pages.title: Arches of Yarn
pages.extract:
{{Stub}} {{Version|2.0.5}} [[File:AOY Oliver Endless Hallway.png|thumb|The Library in Arches of Yarn]] Arches of Yarn is a hidden story produced by collecting [[Items#Book|books]] and [[Items#Manuscript|manuscripts]] within the [[Library]]. There are a total of 45 unique stories that can be read, following two main perspectives: '''Oliver''' and '''Wilbur''', divided across the middle of the index screen. == Indexes == There are 256 unique indexes (0-255) which any Book can have. Only 45 (1-45) will provide a readable story. Manuscripts, on the otherhand, only provide one of the 45 indexes when used. If all indexes are unlocked using the Manuscripts, then the Player will receive the advancement '''{{tooltip|It has been a pleasure.|Collect all of the Library's manuscripts.}}''' These indexes are persistent per instance, meaning loading into a new world under the same Minecraft instance will load the same indexes in the current world. However, these indexes are unique per player, meaning that they do not unlock for everyone if unlocked for one player. == Key == Within the story of Oliver (§1) * Henry / The Beast (§4) * Wilbur (§5) * Young Wilbur (§D) * The "Beast" (§A) * The Library (§2) * Arches of Yarn (§6) == Notes == * The word "house" in [[#Wilbur 12|Wilbur 12]] is marked blue, the same as Oliver, although it has been confirmed not to be Oliver's home. ** This instead is a reference to '''House of Leaves'''. * The Forum user [[themanwhowas]] is heavily implied to have some relation to Arches of Yarn. Most of the contents of this page are from game files and official TBS Discord server.

== In the mod files ==

pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}}
[[File:Backrooms.png|thumb|The Backrooms]]

The '''Backrooms''' is a liminal space, accessible at chance by suffocating inside another block, so long as [[Funny Setting]]s are on.

== Mechanic ==
=== Map Failure ===
While within the '''Backrooms''', most standard maps will fail to properly function.

== Rooms ==
There are 2 variants of the main room type in the '''Backrooms''': Dark and Stained Rooms. These are not exclusive, and can overlap.

=== Stained ===
Stained rooms feature red-tinted blocks instead of the yellow and white of the standard room. 

Stained wallpaper in this room show the word "DIE" along the centers.

=== Dark ===
Dark rooms simply lack any light source found from the Ceiling Lights.

== Exit ==
Dying returns the player to the Overworld.

pages.title: Banning
pages.extract:
{{Stub|Pre 2.0.5 documentation needed + Ban causes}}
{{Version|2.0.5}}
[[File:Banned.png|thumb|Banned!]]
'''Banning''' in context to The Broken Script refers to the mod's ability to ban the Player from a world, '''even in singleplayer'''. It is considered the highest level of punishment the mod can offer.

== Mechanics ==
Banning is caused when [[Revuxor]] appears at the Player's location, typically moments before the Player is killed by an entity. 

=== Pre-2.0 ===
Being banned results in near-complete loss of the world. The only way to be unbanned is by deleting the "entities" folder in the world's file as Revuxor will continue to kick the player upon joining it.

=== 2.0 ===
Bans after the ''2.0 Update'' are much easier to recover from. By disabling banning in the configuration, a Player could rejoin their world without any further consequences

=== 2.0.5+ ===
Banning was reworked and can no longer be disabled in the configs. Upon re-entering the world, the world will begin loading as normal, with the addition of a small message at the top right corner:
* You'll turn out like them.
* Please leave.
* I'm trying to save you.
* Leave now, before it's too late.
* You can still live.
* You've seen the truth like I have. Don't make the same mistake I did.

Once loaded, the Player will be presented with yet another ban screen, only different. It features the current version's panorama with the text '''Connection Lost''' and '''You are banned from this server''' beneath it. This screen also include 3 buttons:
* Attempt Reconnection
* Back to title screen
* Open report directory
'''Back to title screen''' does as intended, and '''Open report directory''' does nothing.
<gallery>False Ban.png|False Ban screen</gallery>

Choosing '''Attempt Reconnection''' will change the button's text to '''I warned you.''' in a white static text, likely a message from [[Revuxor]]. Additionally, the ban lines above change to '''Connection Re-established''' and '''It's your choice.''' respectively.
[[File:I Warned You.png|[[Revuxor]]'s warning]]

After around 5 seconds, the Player will be transported back to either their bed, or the world's spawn.

pages.title: Bobick
pages.extract:
{{Non-canon warning}} {{Entity infobox |title=Bobick |image= {{GalleryHelper |BobickOutline.png¦Bobick¦Bobick tomorrow |Mark101_Bobick.png¦Mark101's Entity¦Original appearance }} |Type=[[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] }} '''Bobick''' is a minor Void Creature adapted from one of unnamed entities that briefly appeared in The Bottom of the Void (mark101) ARG. He was discovered and named by members of the Russian-speaking segment of TBS community, after which he quickly became a fan-favorite in the entire community. A 3D model was created for him by Wendigo, and Bobick himself received positive acknowledgement from the development team as a whole. Bobick was considered to be added to TBS 2.0 back during its development, giving rise to the popular phrase "Bobick tomorrow". Unfortunately, however, mark101 denied permission to use the original entity's design, so in 2.0 release remained only a mention of Bobick as an easter egg in the form of a possible splash text. == Appearance == Bobick is a pitch-black entity made out of wires, with a noticeably blocky build. He's really short, standing at approximately just below 2 blocks tall. He has a small triangular head. == Fanon Behaviour == '''Taken from the suggestion by one of community members.''' Power level: Not as deadly as the void creatures we know, but it can cause a lot of problems if you neglect it. He is unable to absorb the player's soul on his own or get out into reality, but he can damage the player and the world, making him more vulnerable to others. It has the ability to disguise itself into small creatures (similar in size to it) Unlike the void trio led by Integrity, he came by himself. It can only appear if there is a hole in the void in the world (a deleted chunk or a void hole). Behavour Ambushing. If there is a group of small creatures next to the player (chickens, dogs, cats, parrots, etc), then he can appear disguised as such a creature near this group. If a player gets too close to him, he starts attacking. If you kill him before he starts attacking, there is a chance that he will disappear immediately. Attacking. Starts running around the player quickly, dealing 2-3 hearts of damage when hit. He has about 100 health points, and he starts running away if he loses about half of his health. When attacked, it also screams and causes screen glitches (similar to Nothingiswatching) Flee. Starts running away when losing half of his health. It casts a blindness effect on the player and starts running towards the nearest hole into the void. It also summons sub anomalies from time to time. Half a minute later, it disappears, and a new empty hole appears in its place. Staring. ᗽǾᗽĨℂ₭ spawns a couple dozen blocks away from the player and watches him. If you get close to him, he will either disappear or start attacking. However, if you do nothing with it, it will start to cause anomalies. Examples: 1. Stable anomaly - works as a sub-anomaly, but is larger in size and does not move 2. Large hollow holes 2x2 3. Increased chance of shadow bug 4. Replacing random areas with corrupted blocks from Mark101 5. Lift a 5x5x5 cube into the air 6. Nullification (or circuitation) of bread in chests and inventory. 7. Nullification of wheat (you can then make null bread from it :blade:) If it kills the player. Upon death from this entity, the player may receive the following effects for a while (one or more randomly): 1. Screen glitches 2. inability to sleep (err.playerdata.corrupted or something like that) 3. Nullified gui 4. All sounds become a little broken and a tone lower 5. Chat failure 6. Switching some gamerule :tbetroll: 7. inability to run 8. Reduced rendering 9. Lowering the brightness 10. Lock the difficulty to hard 11. Lowering the player's maximum health by several hearts, up to 1/3 of the original. If the player managed to kill him. When he dies, he makes a 7x7 hole in the void, so you're cooked. Interactions with the chat. Bobik Integrity's henchman "Secret" interaction if you try to make fun of his height, he will get very angry and go into an endgame state, increasing to a size of 46 blocks. Your world is cooked and bricked. == Media == Bobick.png|Transparent "Bobick" Render BOBICK_jmih.jpg|Bobick's "introduction". This meme is based on the thumbnail for a video of the same name created by the Russian YouTuber WorldBegemotKot, who tells scary stories. {{Stub}}Cave Base is another clan base belonging to [[Lore#Blackout's Clan|Blackout's Clan]]. It can only spawn underground (though it can spawn partially aboveground; this is presumed to be a bug). Due to how this structure generates, a minimap mod or a large scale excavation is usually required to find it. It contains eight rooms - three belonging to players, two storage rooms, a Nether portal room, a clan rules room, and a room with a protected void block in it.

=== Clan Rules room ===
A room containing the clan rules, which are laid out on signs, and some information about the clan. It has blue wool inlaid in a pattern on the floor and ceiling, as well as four "support beams", one placed in each corner of the room.
[[File:ClanRulesRoom.png|none|thumb|317x317px|Room itself]]

==== <big>Signs in the room</big> ====
'''Center wall signs:'''
 Welcome to the best clan on the server!
 We always welcome new players
 We can give you resources too!
 If you want to join us read clan rules and ask
 __Blackout__
[[File:Clanrulesfrontwall.png|none|thumb|Front wall]]


'''Right wall signs:'''
 Rules
 1 - Don't insult other clan members
 2 - Play minimum 1 hour per day
 3 - Don't grief (If __Blackout__ doesn't say so)
 4 - Don't steal other members resources
 5 - Be active
 6 - Have fun!
[[File:Clanrulessigns.png|none|thumb|Rules wall]]

=== Clan storage room ===
A room containing four double chests and two chests.
[[File:Storageroomblackoutbase.png|none|thumb|Clan storage room.]]

=== Nether Portal room ===
A room containing a Nether Portal and nothing else.
[[File:Blackoutbase nether portal.png|none|thumb|The Nether portal room. Very small!]]

=== OVERLORD's room ===
A room belonging to one of Blackout's clan members. It contains a white bed with two furnaces and a crafting table placed above it, a jukebox containing the disc for [[Items#Record 14|Record 14]], two double chests, and two chests. One chest in this room contains several stacks of oak planks, another copy of Record 14, six redstone torches, a stack of glass, and an oak door. All other chests contain name.null. The furnaces contain nothing.
[[File:OVERLORD's room.png|none|thumb|OVERLORD's room]]
[[File:OVERLORDchest.png|none|thumb|Chest in room containing Record 14]]

=== Weird Block room ===
A room containing several signs and a protected void block.
[[File:Nefarious block room.png|none|thumb|The nefarious block room]]

==== <big>Signs in the room</big> ====
 |4.8.2019 What is it?
 |4.8.2019 I dunno, I found it in some cave and moved it here
 using pistons

 |4.8.2018 btw where is blackout?
[[File:Signsblockroom1.png|none|thumb|225x225px|Signs detailing a conversation]]
[[File:Signsblockroom2.png|none|thumb|244x244px|Sign asking where Blackout is]]

=== catfish12's room ===
A room belonging to one of Blackout's clan members. It contains a red bed, three furnaces, a crafting table, two chests and two double chests. The furnaces each have one stack of name.null inside.
[[File:Catfish12roomwoah.png|none|thumb|catfish12's room.]]

=== Blackout's room ===
A room belonging to Blackout. It is the most decorated of the rooms, containing red and orange carpets as well as a lamp with a lever and trapdoors on the wall. It also contains two furnaces, a crafting table, a red bed, four double chests, an anvil, six bookshelves, and an enchanting table.
[[File:Blackoutroomwaow.png|none|thumb|Blackout's room.]]

{{Entity infobox |title=Chord |image= {{GalleryHelper |Chord-yester7render.png¦Piano Chord }} |Nicknames= |Role= |Type=[[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] |Affiliations=[[Void]] |HP=32 |Armor=0 }} '''Chord''' is a [[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] that appears exclusively as a summon during [[Integrity#First phase|Phase 1]] of the [[Integrity]] bossfight. According to lore, a '''Chord''' is the split form of the collective entity '''Harmony''', a single entity capable of splitting itself into smaller entities known as Chords. The reason for its splitting during the events of the mod is currently unknown. When Integrity finishes its pre-battle speech, it summons a group of 10 Chords that hover in the air above the arena. Players cannot damage Integrity itself during this phase; the only path forward is to slay every Chord. Once the last surviving Chord dies, the boss automatically transitions into Phase 2. == Appearance == Chord is a moderate-sized void creature whose hitbox is approximately 2×2 blocks. Its head bears a four-pointed-star texture and constantly rotates to face the player, giving the impression of a star-shaped silhouette. Long void tendrils hang from the underside of the head, and two pairs of tendrils extend outward from the sides as wings. == Stats == Chord is a boss-fight summon and therefore has modest raw stats: * '''Maximum health''':32 * '''Attack damage (laser)''':4 * '''Attack damage (projectile)''': 2 * '''Follow range''': 50 blocks * '''Movement speed''': 1 * '''Flying speed''': 10 * '''Hitbox''': 2×2 blocks * '''Armor''': 0 * '''Knockback resistance''': Standard * '''XP reward''': 0 Chords can be damaged and killed by standard weapons. == Behaviour == === Flight AI === Each Chord uses a custom three-state flight controller: * '''Approaching''': When the player is more than 12 blocks away, the Chord moves toward the player and hovers 8 blocks above their head * '''Holding''': When the player is between 4 and12 blocks away, the Chord maintains roughly8-block distance * '''Retreating''': When the player is closer than 4 blocks, the Chord decelerates (×0.85 speed) to keep distance === Targeting === Chord retains a lock on its target player for up to 200 ticks (10 seconds) after losing line of sight, continuing to pursue throughout that window. === Combat === Each Chord is randomly assigned one of two attack types at generation: '''Laser type''' * Charges for about 1 second, accompanied by a piano chord note, then fires a red laser at the player's last recorded position * The laser deals '''4 damage''' to anything within about half a block of the targeted point '''Projectile type''' * Fires a [[#Chord Projectile|Chord Projectile]] directly at the player (speed1.6), dealing '''2 damage''' on contact * The projectile despawns on contact with another Chord — you can exploit this by baiting two projectiles into each other * The projectile also despawns after traveling 100 blocks The Chord occasionally switches to melee charge mode for roughly one second, accelerating straight at the player. If it reaches melee range it lands a strike, so maintaining distance is the safest option. == Death == Chord plays a death animation of 78 ticks (3.9 seconds) before being removed server-side. When struck, Chord plays the same sound effects as its death (a random pick from chord_death_1-4.ogg) at a slightly higher pitch (×1.35) to distinguish it from a killing blow. Chord drops neither items nor experience. == Chord Projectile == The '''Chord Projectile''' is a custom projectile fired by projectile-type Chords: * '''Gravity''': None — flies in a straight line * '''Speed''': 1.6 * '''Damage''': 2 base * '''Lifetime''': Auto-discards after 100 blocks * '''Friendly-fire protection''': Disappears on contact with another Chord == Notes == * Chords make piano sounds for all their actions, which is consistent with the musical naming of Chord and Harmony. * Chord's head design appears to be inspired by a scrapped redesign of [[Sub Anomaly 1]]. * Each Chord is randomly assigned its attack type (laser or projectile) at generation time and retains it for the entire fight — it never switches types mid-fight. * A reliable strategy is to focus fire on one Chord at a time, since killing one reduces the tracking burden on the player and decreases the number of projectiles to dodge. * Chord's spawn sounds have ''Instability'''s leitmotif. == Media == |-|Gallery= chordwikitransparent.png|Transparent Chord Render |-|Menu Fanart= baby_harmony.jpg|Menu Fanart chords_now_3d.png|Menu Fanart coordinates.jpg|Menu Fanart |-|Animations Outlined= File:chord-attack-jelly_w.gif|Projectile Attack File:chord-attack-laser_w.gif|Laser Attack File:chord-damaged_w.gif|Damaged File:chord-damaged-v2_w.gif|Damaged v2 File:chord-death_w.gif|Death File:chord-flying_w.gif|Flying File:chord-idle_w.gif|Idle File:chord-sapwn_w.gif|Spawn |-|Animations No Outline= File:chord-attack-jelly.gif|Projectile Attack File:chord-attack-laser.gif|Laser Attack File:chord-damaged.gif|Damaged File:chord-damaged-v2.gif|Damaged v2 File:chord-death.gif|Death File:chord-flying.gif|Flying File:chord-idle.gif|Idle File:chord-sapwn.gif|Spawn |-|Sounds= Shoot {{Clear}} [[File:Chord_shoot_1.ogg]]

}}{{Quote
| text = Do not make me wake the others.
| author = Circuit after revealing himself from his disguise
}}'''Circuit''' is an intelligent [[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] that is the '''lowest''' in the chain of command.

He is the primary murderer of [[Lore#Clans|Clan Server]] as the one who killed most of them, with Null even claiming it was all his fault. One of the things Circuit did was '''infiltrate [[xXram2dieXx_(Lore)|xXram2dieXx's]] clan''' after he went missing. He '''disguised as''' [[xXram2dieXx_(Lore)|xXram2dieXx]] and “returned” to the server on 06.09.2019. Circuit justified xXram2dieXx's absence by blaming it on “troubles with his family”. Another, but more gruesome one, is that Circuit '''killed [[Revuxor]] in real life''', having broken out of Revuxor's computer screen, before hunting Revuxor down in his own home and '''ripping him apart'''.

He '''usually appears underground''', with different behaviors depending on certain conditions such as {{mcw|altitude}} and {{mcw|Cave biomes|biome}}. However, he may also appear on the surface, '''[[#Disguised|disguising]] himself''' as any mob or in stalking form.

== Appearance ==
He is a pitch-black, wire-like entity with a rhombus-shaped head. He stands approximately 7 blocks tall. He has an awkward upright standing gait and is frequently observed skittering around on all fours. 

In 2.0, Circuit's appearance was overhauled, giving him a more proportionate body and thickening the tendrils that make up his body. He now has bones, most notably a ribcage, but also something of a pelvis, although busted. He was also made 3D, unlike his previous model, which was 2D.

== Personality ==
{{Quote
| text = It was all his fault.
| author = [[Null]] when spoken to about Circuit.
}}
Unlike the other void creatures, there is very little to go off of in terms of speech, though based on his actions, it's shown that Circuit is quite malevolent and dangerous due to having the most confirmed victims of any other Void Creature and being responsible for the downfall of the Clan Server. Despite being more feral than the others he is quite intelligent, being able to speak, shapeshift into mobs and players to mess with his victims, and hide himself amongst groups such as when he took the form of a missing [[xXram2dieXx]] and impersonated him. 

He is also extremely violent, shown that his method is killing is brutally tearing apart the victim.  

He may or may not have a particular and morbid interest in [[DyeXD412]] for unknown reasons, as its heavily implied that Circuit is now using his [[Curved|body as a puppet]]. Before 2.0 one of the results of a Mineshaft Circuit encounter was [[Curved]] spawning.

== Behaviour ==
=== Chase ===
He will enter an upright position and begin his intro animation for the next {{tooltip|8 seconds|160 ticks}}, playing <ab>circuit_intro.ogg</ab>'''circuit_intro.ogg''' if he has line of sight with a Player. 

In some cases, Circuit may instead spawn much faster, playing <ab>fast_circuit_intro.ogg</ab>'''fast_circuit_intro.ogg''' and only taking {{tooltip|3 seconds|60 ticks}} to begin his chase.

Once his intro is complete, '''<ab>circuit_chase.ogg</ab>circuit_chase.ogg.''' will begin playing and will loop until the chase is over.

If Circuit sees the Player, he will begin to approach at a rapid rate, playing <ab>circuit_jumpscare.ogg</ab>'''circuit_jumpscare.ogg''' if immediately his intro just finished. Otherwise, he will wander randomly until either the chase ends or he finds the Player.

Additionally, the Game Window title will change to "YOU CAN'T ESCAPE YOU CAN'T ESCAPE YOU CAN'T ESCAPE"

Circuit will '''climb over blocks''' in order to reach the player. If there are blocks in his way while climbing, Circuit will break them '''regardless of what they are'''.

Circuit can also '''swim faster''' than a Player with Depth Strider III. 

If Circuit has line of sight with the Player during a chase, the Pause Menu will be altered as well. The word "Paused" now corrupted, and the "Save and Quit to Title" option, once clicked, becomes corrupted, falling off of the Pause Menu.

If Circuit knows where the Player is, the UI will begin to shake rapidly.

Every {{tooltip|2.25 seconds|45 ticks}} each of the following will happen if Circuit can see the Player:
* Red text with the phrase '''There is no way out''' will jump across the screen. 
* <ab>circuit_jumpscare.ogg</ab>'''circuit_jumpscare.ogg''' will play at a random speed and pitch
* [[#/media/File:Screenshot_2025-01-01_145155.png|screenshot_2025-01-01_145155.png]] will appear for {{tooltip|0.1 seconds|2 ticks}}
* With a 70% chance, the time will be faked to midnight, and a black screen will appear for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}
* With a 70% chance, the time will be faked to midnight, and [[#/media/File:JFrame2.png|frame 2 of JFrame]] will appear for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}
* With a 70% chance, the time will be faked to day.

If Circuit catches the Player, they will be kicked (if Enabled) with the message "No more running" or "No more hiding" and killed. The death message will read '''<player> couldn't hide.''' 

He will disappear {{tooltip|40 seconds|800 ticks}} after spawning in.

=== Cave ===
Circuit can only spawn if he does not already exist somewhere, if the biome is not {{mcw|Deep Dark}}, if the sky is not visible where he is to spawn, if the {{mcw|y-level}} of the place he is trying to spawn at is below 30, and if the player's {{mcw|y-level}} is below 40. He has a 99% chance of instantly despawning.

Upon spawning he will play either <ab>falsecalm2.ogg</ab>'''falsecalm2.ogg''' with a 70% chance, or <ab>integritywatching.ogg</ab>'''integritywatching.ogg''' with a 30% chance.

Circuit will appear standing at his full height.

If the player gets within '''{{tooltip|5 blocks|10x10x10 cube}}''' or directly look at any variant of a '''Cave''' Circuit, one of the following will happen:

* Circuit will begin to [[#Chase|Chase]] the player
* A black screen will appear for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}. Circuit will disappear, playing a sound effect.

He will disappear {{tooltip|8 minutes and 20 seconds|10000 ticks}} after spawning.

==== Stalk ====
Circuit will begin to slowly approach the player.

==== Stare ====
Circuit will stand in place, watching the player.

=== Mineshaft ===
Circuit can only spawn if he does not already exist somewhere, if the sky is not visible where he is to spawn, if the {{mcw|y-level}} of the place he is trying to spawn at is above 30, and if the player's {{mcw|y-level}} is above 40. 

Also an additional requirement is the presence of at least one oak planks block in a {{tooltip|3 block radius|6x6x6 cube}} around his spawn location, where for each block found Circuit has a 10% chance to spawn.

Circuit will appear standing on all fours.

Upon spawning he will play an eerie noise.

He will disappear {{tooltip|8 minutes and 20 seconds|10000 ticks}} after spawning, regardless of his active behaviour.

==== Stare ====
Circuit will stand in place, watching the player.

If the player gets within '''{{tooltip|5 blocks|10x10x10 cube}}''' or directly look at Circuit, one of the following will happen:

* Circuit will begin to [[#Chase|Chase]] the player
* A black screen will appear for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}. Circuit will disappear, playing a sound effect.

==== Walk ====
Circuit will begin to rapidly approach the player, moving at the same speed as the player while sprinting.

Looking at Circuit will scare him away, prompting him to [[#Flee|Flee]].

If the player fails to look at Circuit while he is in his Walk state and Circuit touches them, 2 - 2.5 hearts of damage will be dealt to the player every second.

If within '''{{tooltip|5 blocks|10x10x10 cube}}''' and looking at Circuit, he will either [[#Chase|Chase]] or disappear.

==== Flee ====
Circuit will skitter away from the player and after {{tooltip|15 seconds|300 ticks}} will switch back to his [[#Walk|Walk]] behavior, accommodated by an eerie noise.

=== Disguised ===
Circuit has the ability to shapeshift into various forms, mostly mobs and player-like forms.

==== Deceiver ====
During the night, '''a chat message''' can appear stating that a Player has just joined the game.

The Deceiver will appear somewhere nearby '''wearing the same armor as the real Player''', holding an Iron Sword, Iron Axe, Iron Shovel, or Iron Pickaxe. If the real Player removes their armor, it will reveal the Deceiver's skin is '''pitch-black''', reminiscent of [[Null]]. The real Player re-equipping their armor will '''not''' re-equip the Deceiver's armor.

The Deceiver will run after the player. If he gets within 5 blocks radius of the player, he will disappear playing <ab>circuit_deceive.ogg</ab>'''circuit_deceive.ogg''', after which one of the following will happen:
* With a 70% chance, Circuit will switch the Player's gamemode to survival and appear, entering into a [[#Chase|Fast Chase]].
* With a 30% chance, nothing happens.

The Deceiver will disappear during the day.

==== Fake Player ====
During the night, a fake Player can appear somewhere nearby, '''disguised as the Player or another Player they have played with''' recently, accompanied by a message saying "<player> has joined the game".

This variant is much more dangerous than the Deceiver, as the Circuit will mimic the same skin, nametag, and armor as the Player they are mimicking. They do not disappear during the day. 

The fake player will '''approach the Player''', and upon getting close enough, will attach himself to one of the Player's directions and mimic the players movement and rotations. 

After some time has passed in this state, or if ever damaged, Circuit will reveal himself and enter into a [[#Chase|Fast Chase]].

==== Inhabited Mobs ====
Circuit can spawn on the surface, inhabiting and disguised as any mob in the game.

After the ''2.0 Update'', these disguises are visually indistinguishable from their real counterparts, as it is based off of an entity property, instead of having their own entities types.

These mobs will additionally function the same as their real counterpart. Actions such as breeding pigs, trading with villagers, and other mob specific interactions will work as intended.   

All Circuit inhabited mobs will attempt to stay within '''15 blocks''' of the Player, and will often stop to look directly at the Player.

If attacked by a Player's melee attack, regardless of the damage, Circuit will reveal himself and enter a [[#Chase|Fast Chase]]. If Circuit is unable to enter chase with the Player, the attack will instead deal the intended damage.

Certain mobs that are inhabited by Circuit will become aggressive towards the Player, including '''Iron Golems and tamed mobs'''. These mobs will attack the Player if outside of this range until stopped, or the distance to the Player is less than 15 blocks.

Tamed mobs, such as Wolves, Cats, or Parrots, will approach the player '''even while they are seated''' if the Player is outside this 15 block range.

Iron Golems will '''never''' attack a Circuit if it is inhabited.

==== Ore Circuit ====
Very rarely, mining an ore block can spawn Circuit, entering into a [[#Chase|Fast Chase]].

=== Ceiling ===
Circuit follows standard spawn conditions in this form. This form can spawn through [[Random Events#Circuit Ceiling|a random event]], or naturally; however, a natural spawn enters [[#Chase|Chase]] as soon as it spawns.

Circuit will initially wait idly until a player is in their line in sight, where they will approach the player as long as the player has seen Circuit once.

Once their destination was reached, Circuit will then enter a [[#Chase|Fast Chase]].

He will despawn {{tooltip|3 minutes and 30 seconds|4200 ticks}} after spawning in.

== Notes ==
* Though Void Creatures canonically lack gender identities or a biological sex, Circuit is referred to as he/him pronouns by his victims and the developers.
* Circuit was supposed to have a minigame where, when a player was caught, as one of the outcomes he would give them 60 seconds to get to the surface, instead of instantly switching to his '''Chase''' behavior.
** The speech audio files '''circuitminigamespeechandcounting.ogg''' and '''circuitspeechbadending.ogg''' are now used for [[Integrity]] as '''integrityspeechandcounting.ogg''' and '''integrityendgamespeech.ogg'''.
* From 1.9.3 onwards, if the player tries to enable devmode and enters the code 2018, '''1000''' Circuits with '''Chase''' behavior will instantly spawn on the player's location with the intent of lagging the player's game; devmode otherwise works as expected.
* If you delete circuit_dance.gif file in the mod file, the game will not work properly and crash.  The crash title reads "They're so joyous..." and the exception is "Get it, circy! Crash their game!". Quite funny.
* Before 2.0, if Circuit was disguised as a mob, it would appear with that mob's custom icon while holding Tab with ''Xaero's Map'' and/or ''Xaero's Minimap''. This allowed for safely checking if a Pig, Villager or Creeper is false, as you could monitor its movement (they are significantly faster than their real counterpart) to judge them without Circuit being in danger range or visible at all. This was removed with the 2.0 update as entities will no longer appear on any of ''Xaero's'' map mods.
** If one was using the ''Creepers Overhaul'' mod, a false Creeper was easily distinguishable as default Creepers lack an icon.
** Keeping Villagers safely stored in your base is a good way to keep track of true Villagers, as any other Villager outside where they're kept is most likely a Circuit.
* Circuit's chase theme is a heavily remixed and reversed version of Abandoned Kerfur's Phase 3 theme from Voices of the Void

{{Version|2.0.5}} '''Clan Void''' is a dimension that is composed of 5 layers. From top to bottom these layers are: Day A, Stone, Wood, Maze, and Clan Void. To prevent confusion between the Clan Void dimension and the Clan Void layer, the layer will be referred to as "Clan Void (Layer)." Entering the Clan Void can be done through either entering [[431434]] or interacting with [[Notexture]] at a 25% chance. Upon entering the Clan Void, the Player will be transported to one of the layers at random, with exception of [[#Stone|Stone]]. Each layer has a unique room or structure that contains a chest with one of the five Polaroid Pieces. There are only one of each piece in a world and the coordinates of the pieces are given via specific events that can occur. See more [[Progression#Polaroid Pieces|here.]] == Mechanics == === Ambience === As long as the Player is in the dimension, ambient audio will play, dependent on the layer the Player is on. ==== Day A ==== While on this layer, 1 of 5 tracks will begin playing. The tracks are all distorted versions of songs from the Minecraft soundtrack by C418, labeled as cursed_music. Day A Excuse.ogg|'''excuse.ogg''' Day A Haggstrom.ogg|'''haggstrom.ogg''' Day A Living Mice.ogg|'''living_mice.ogg''' Day A Minecraft.ogg|'''minecraft.ogg''' Day A Sweden.ogg|'''sweden.ogg''' ==== Stone ==== While on this layer, '''stone.ogg''' will play. Stone.ogg|'''Stone.ogg''' ==== Wood ==== Instead of looping music, various sound effects can be heard at random. woodsfx1.ogg|'''woodsfx1.ogg''' woodsfx2.ogg|'''woodsfx2.ogg''' ==== Maze ==== Instead of looping music, various sound effects can be heard at random. mazesfx1.ogg|'''mazesfx1.ogg''' mazesfx2.ogg|'''mazesfx2.ogg''' ==== Clan Void ==== No ambience is played in the Clan Void (Layer) === Teleportation === '''Clan Void''' can teleport the Player between different areas, dependent on their actions. * At chance, when entering [[53135Exit6436]], the Player can be transported into another layer of the '''Clan Void'''. This does '''not''' happen with items or other entities, as they will stay at the intended positions. It is not recommended to drop important items or entities within this dimension. == Day A == {{Hatnote|'''Day A''' redirects here. For the dimension, see [[Day A_(Dimension)|here]]}} [[File:Day A 2.0.png|thumb|Day A]] Day A is first and topmost layer of the Clan Void, sitting at Y = 252. Accessing it can be accomplished by digging up from the Stone layer below or from falling in the void in this dimension. Day A resembles a superflat world with oak trees and grass present throughout the layer. The area surrounding the Player is covered in white fog in comparison to the other layers which have pitch black fog. Day A has the most unique structures out of the 5 layers, consisting mostly of bases along with other structures such as large oak trees, houses, or other misc features. This layer also contains 2 biomes: '''Day A''' and '''Day A Alpha'''. The Alpha variant appears to match the brighter more saturated colours of Alpha Minecraft, and features red & cyan roses, though both are called "Rose" The Stone layer can be accessed by mining the bedrock below the grass. This is the only layer in which the player can mine directly through the floor to reach the next layer. === Structures === ==== 0nullvoid0's Base ==== [[XXram2dieXx (Lore)|xXram2dieXx]]'s base prior to the creation of [[Clan Build]], and even before his name change (0nullvoid0). ty |??? |tek_woodfloor29 | |- |} == Maze == Maze is the fourth layer of the Clan Void at Y = 207. The Maze layer, as name implies, is a cobblestone maze with very little light, making [[Null#Maze|Null]] much easier to spot. The layer can lead to Day A and Clan Void layer through the Clan Void Intersection, or up to Wood layer through tek_woodfloor5 or woodfloorintersection === Rooms === [[File:Clan Void Maze Layer.png|none|thumb|Maze]] ==== clandimensionroom1 ==== This room is one piece of the maze. ==== clandimensionroom2 ==== This room is one piece of the maze. ==== clandimensionroom3 ==== This room is one piece of the maze. ==== clandimensionroom4 ==== This room continues the maze, but contains 3 doorways to another room. The two small doorways have obfuscated signs at their entrance which read "aAAAAA". This subroom contains a 7x7 wall of '''53135Exit6436 blocks''', acting as the only exit from this layer. Additionally, there are 3 furnaces, a crafting table, and 12 chests, containing a total of 975 '''name.null'''. [[File:clandimensionroom4.png|none|thumb|Maze Room 4]] [[File:AAAAA_sign.png|none|thumb|aAAAAA]] ==== clandimensionroom5 ==== This room contains 4 cobblestone hourglasses structures, irregularly set in the room. ==== clan_void_intersection ==== This room contains 4 entrances, and a lower level leading to 4 exits into the Clan Void layer. Dropping down further into the void will send the Player above the Day A layer. [[File:clan_void_intersection.png|none|thumb|Clan Void Intersection]] ==== mazepredetermined (Polaroid Room) ==== This room contains a large pyramid of cobblestone, with a double chest sitting on the top of it. The chest contains '''Polaroid Piece 2''', 18 '''name.null''', and 27 '''name.revuxor'''. [[File:mazepredetermined.png|none|thumb|Maze Predetermined]] [[File:polaroid piece 2 chest.png|none|thumb|Polaroid chest.]] === Gallery === clandimensionroom1_render.png|Maze Room 1 clandimensionroom2_render.png|Maze Room 2 clandimensionroom3_render.png|Maze Room 3 clandimensionroom4_render.png|Maze Room 4 clandimensionroom5_render.png|Maze Room 5 == Clan Void (Layer) == Clan Void (Layer) is the fifth and bottom layer of the Clan Void at Y = 201. Unlike the rest of the layers, the Clan Void (Layer) does not contain [[53135Exit6436]]. The only way to exit the Clan Void (Layer) is through the Maze layer intersection, where the Player can continue up through the Maze, or jump into the void and teleport to the topmost layer. === Rooms === There are a total of 13 different rooms in the Clan Void dimension, these are the following: ==== clanvoidnew1 (Hub Room) ==== This room is completely empty, the default version of the other rooms. [[File:clanvoidnew1.png|none|thumb|Hub Room]] ==== clanvoidnew2 (IKNOWWHATYOUFEAR) ==== This room features a set of doors at each entrance, and obfuscated signs which read "IKNOWWHATYOUFEAR" [[File:clanvoidnew2.png|none|thumb|Main Room]] [[File:iknowwhatyoufear_sign.png|none|thumb|IKNOWWHATYOUFEAR]] ==== clanvoidnew3 (Pillar Room) ==== This room features cobblestone pillars with smooth stone slab supports. [[File:Clan void-pillars room.png|none|thumb|Pillar room]] ==== clanvoidnew4 (Storage Room) ==== This room has empty double chests, 4 in each corner. [[File:Clan void-storage room.png|none|thumb|Storage room]] ==== clanvoidnew5 (Utility Room) ==== This room has 2 furnaces and 1 crafting table in each corner of the room. [[File:Clan void-furnace room.png|none|thumb|Utility room]] ==== clanvoidnew6 (Disc 13 Room) ==== This room has 4 cobblestone wall pillars with 4 double chests and 4 jukeboxes in the center. Each double chest is filled with Disc 13. [[File:Clan void-disc room.png|none|thumb|Disc 13 Room]] ==== clanvoidnew7 (Crafting Room) ==== This room contains a structure made out of 48 crafting tables resembling a support frame. [[File:Clan void-crafting room.png|none|thumb|Crafting Room]] ==== clanvoidnew8 (Exit Room) ==== An unused room, completely filled with '''53135Exit6436 blocks'''. [[File:Clan void-exit room.png|none|thumb|Exit Room]] ==== clanvoidnew9 (Pole Room) ==== This room features cobblestone pillars with smooth stone bottom caps. [[File:Clan void-pole room.png|none|thumb|Pole Room]] ==== clanvoidnew10 (Carpet Room) ==== This room features a red carpet pathway in a plus shape. Redstone lanterns are in each top corner of the room. [[File:Clan void-carpet room.png|none|thumb|Exit Carpet]] ==== clanvoidnew11 (Farm Room) ==== A small wheat farm in each corner of the room. [[File:Clan void-farm room.png|none|thumb|Farm Room]] ==== clanvoidnew12 (Fate Room) ==== A series of 8 redstone torches surround the center of the room. Over the glass are signs, reading the lines "Just close your eyes and wait", similar to that of the rooftop of the [[Clan Build]] [[File:Clan void-fate room.png|none|thumb|Fate Room]] [[File:Clan void-fate room_signs.png|none|thumb|Just close your eyes and wait]] ==== clanvoidnew13 (Trance Room) ==== Featuring wooden archways at the entrance, this room is the only room to contain the '''glass border blocks'''. Looking up will show the stars and various blocks falling. [[File:Clan void-trance room.png|none|thumb|Trance Room]] [[File:Clan void-trance room_extra.png|none|thumb|Looking up at the glass]] ==== clan_void_rooms ==== This room contains 4 sub-rooms, with 2 single door entrances into them. There are 10 different sub-rooms. [[File:clan_void_rooms.png|none|thumb|Clan Void Rooms]] ==== clan_void_subroom_1 ==== This subroom contains a cobblestone fractal, torches occupying the bottom two cobblestone. [[File:clan_void_subroom_1.png|none|thumb|Subroom 1]] ==== clan_void_subroom_2 ==== This subroom contains a small pond of water in a plus shape, held together with glass. [[File:clan_void_subroom_2.png|none|thumb|Subroom 2]] ==== clan_void_subroom_3 ==== This subroom contains a pillar of flowing lava by the roof, encased in glass. [[File:clan_void_subroom_3.png|none|thumb|Subroom 3]] ==== clan_void_subroom_4 ==== This subroom contains oak fences connecting to two central cobblestone blocks. [[File:clan_void_subroom_4.png|none|thumb|Subroom 4]] ==== clan_void_subroom_5 ==== This subroom contains alternating pillars of brick and glass. [[File:clan_void_subroom_5.png|none|thumb|Subroom 5]] ==== clan_void_subroom_6 ==== This subroom contains a structure of oak planks [[File:clan_void_subroom_6.png|none|thumb|Subroom 6]] ==== clan_void_subroom_7 ==== This subroom contains a floor of oak planks, red carpet, and torches by the roof. [[File:clan_void_subroom_7.png|none|thumb|Subroom 7]] ==== clan_void_subroom_8 ==== This subroom contains a floor of oak planks, and orange and yellow carpet in a checkered board pattern [[File:clan_void_subroom_8.png|none|thumb|Subroom 8]] ==== clan_void_subroom_9 ==== This subroom contains 4 pillars of furnaces and one of lava sources in the center. [[File:clan_void_subroom_9.png|none|thumb|Subroom 9]] ==== clan_void_subroom_0 ==== This subroom contains a pillar of Crafting Tables. [[File:clan_void_subroom_0.png|none|thumb|Subroom 0]] ==== clan_void_intersection ==== This room is similar to the Clan Void Rooms Unlike other rooms mentioned above, this room is completely made out of cobblestone and contains a second level. All 8 entrances into this room are connected by a set of doors. Going up will lead to the Maze layer, while dropping down into the void will send the Player above the Day A layer. [[File:clan_void_intersection.png|none|thumb|Clan Void Intersection]] ==== clan_void_predetermined (Polaroid Room) ==== This room contains a single double chest, in it containing '''Polaroid Piece 1''', 12 '''name.null''', and 14 '''name.revuxor'''. [[File:clan_void_predetermined.png|none|thumb|Clan Void Predetermined]] [[File:polaroid piece 1 chest.png|none|thumb|Polaroid chest.]] == Exit == Dying within the '''Clan Void''' will send the Player back into the Overworld. Entering [[53135Exit6436]] will also produce the same results, though at chance. It is also possible to be sent back into the Overworld after an amount of time, although this is rare to occur. == Entities == It is possible to encounter [[Null#Maze|Null]] in the Clan Void who will chase the Player. [[Null#Maze|Null]] is able to spawn on all layers, with the exception of [[#Day A|Day A]]. When spawned in the Clan Void, [[Null#Maze|Null]] gives off light starting at a light level of 15, allowing the Player to tell where [[Null#Maze|Null]] is in comparison to the pitch black fog. Upon seeing the Player, [[Null#Maze|Null]] will begin to chase them until either enough distance is made or if the Player kills [[Null#Maze|Null]]. If the Player were to be killed by [[Null#Maze|Null]], they will be given the death message of, "(player) was found." == Notes == * The old version of this dimension (1.9~1.10.1) only had one layer, precisely the "Clan Void" or the current fifth layer. * There is an older version of this dimension before the ''1.9 update'' where the dimension instead was a maze-like medium with a cobblestone roof and floor as well as cobblestone walls and pillars, just like the current maze layer; to leave the dimension in this version, players had to wait a few minutes to get teleported back out. ** In 1.9～1.10.1, That maze can still be encountered under rare circumstances within this dimension, though in most cases the maze remains relatively small and is surrounded by other rooms, making it difficult to discover without breaking through walls. * Before the ''2.0 update'', the Day A layer was its [[Day A (Dimension)|own separate dimension]] from the Clan Void, but has since then been made the topmost layer of the Clan Void dimension. pages.extract: {{Version|2.0.4|major}} The Broken Script contains a lot of commands, almost all of them being for administrators only. == Player commands == === /tbsc === The /tbsc command is seemingly for testing purposes, it is available to all players. It stands for '''TBS Client Commands'''. It previously was one of the ways to modify the configuration of the mod, but as of 2.0 it only has a minimal amount of commands, none of them related to the config. As the name indicates, these commands are not available on a dedicated server. ==== boss_end ==== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Section || start / end || start: plays the end cutscene of the mod, moving the camera up and showing the end credits shortly after. end: Shows the end credits directly, skipping the aforementioned cutscene. |} A test command, likely used to make sure the ending cutscene was working well before release. Source: FinalCutsceneHandler.CUTSCENE.start() / .end(). ==== camera ==== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Axis || z || The axis, only z is available. |- | Amount || Number || The value to override the camera in the specified axis, in radians. |} This command rotates the camera in the specified axis by ''Amount'' radians. Source: CameraZAxisKt.setAngle. ==== figure ==== This command will crash the game as it tries to load a file that is not present in the release versions of TBS. If it were to work, it would open a new [https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/uiswing/components/panel.html Java Swing panel] that would animate a spritesheet located at thebrokenscript/textures/testing/infect_<frame>.png, where <frame> would be a number between 0 and 7 and updated every tick. When the animation would have finished, it would have closed itself and frozen Minecraft for 2 seconds. ==== moonrise ==== Lets you control the ambience of [[Fractured]], even outside of the intended location. ===== init ===== Creates the internal class that handles the Moon Rise ambience (MoonRiseAmbience). ===== stage ===== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Stage || Integer (0-3) || What stage/level to set the ambience to. |} Source: Jimbo.MOONRISE.applyStage(stage). ==== test ==== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Sound || Sound asset || The sound to play. |- | Loop || Boolean || Self explanatory. |- | Volume || Number || How much to increase the base volume by, where 1 = 100%. |- | Pitch || Number || Pitch multiplier, where 1 = 100%. |- | Gain || Number || Additional volume multiplier, setting the gain from the audio engine this time. 1 = 100%. |} Although it looks like a copy of [[https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/playsound|/playsound]], this command uses BrokenCore's Fancy Audio API to play sounds. Source: FancyAudio.play(...).setGain(gain). == Server commands == === /tbs === The /tbs command handles all commands related to the mod's state. These commands are locked behind requiring administrator permissions, whether it'd be through [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/op /op] or the server console. '''Note''': All /tbs dev subcommands require the cheats config to be enabled in BrokenCore (BCConfigs.getEnableCheats), otherwise the command will fail with "Cheats are not enabled!". ==== reputation ==== This command allows you to see your [[reputation]]. As an admin, you can get another player's reputation by using [https://minecraft.wiki/Commands/execute /execute] as <player>. '''Mechanism''' (source): checks PlayerVariables.entityReputation and displays a tier: * Rep ≤ 25 → '''BAD''' (hover text: "Null is pissed and his hatred for you is at maximum. Expect hell from null. Null will now more often attack the player.") * 25 < Rep ≤ 75 → '''NORMAL''' (hover text: "Null and you are neutral between each other. Null can sometimes hurt the player.") * Rep > 75 → '''GOOD''' (hover text: "Null is cool and doesn't care about you being here. Null will rarely hurt the player.") '''Note''': The tier labels (BAD / NORMAL / GOOD), hover descriptions, message prefixes (Reputation value: / Reputation:), and the trailing (hover for more information) hint are all '''hardcoded English strings''' in the source code, not loaded from the lang system. Players will always see English regardless of the resource pack. This command must be executed by a player; running it from the console returns -1. ==== devmode ==== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Code || Integer || The special code to input. |} Allows entering special codes set by the developers. Currently available codes are: * 2018: Spawns 1000 [[Circuit]]s at your current location, printing '''Have fun!''' in the chat/console. * 544253: Spawns 1000 [[The Broken End]]s at your current location, printing '''Have fun!''' in the chat/console. Other codes print "Dev mode code is invalid!". ==== dev ==== Most of the /tbs commands are located in this subcommand. '''Note''': All commands in this category require the cheats config to be enabled in BrokenCore. ===== arena ===== Various commands to test the [[Integrity]] boss fight, this can be used to spawn Integrity in the overworld if you want that for some reason. ====== start ====== Starts the Arena at the player's current location. Success message: '''Have fun...''' ====== create ====== Creates a new Arena instance and adds the current player to the participants list. Success message: '''Created arena!''' ====== next ====== Advances the Arena to the next phase (arena.nextPhase()). Fails if no Arena is active. ====== kill_phase_3 ====== Kills Integrity in Phase 3 of the active Arena (arena.getPhase3().getIntegrity().kill()). Fails if no Arena is active. ====== destroy ====== Destroys the current Arena (arena.reset(); Arena.instance = null). Fails if no Arena is active. ====== arms ====== Spawns the "wacky wavy inflatable gas station arms" in Phase 3. Success message: '''Spawned wacky wavy inflatable gas station arms!''' ===== boss ===== ====== animate ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Entity || The entity to animate. Must be thebrokenscript:integrity_phase_1. |} Forces the Integrity entity to crawl out of the ground via IntegrityPhase1Entity.setCrawlOut(true). Error message: '''Must be integrity, you dumbass!'''. Success message: '''great job''' ====== kit ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Gives the targeted players a full set of '''highest tier items''' for testing the boss fights without having to gear up manually. Items given: * Protection IV Netherite helmet / chestplate / leggings / boots * Sharpness V Netherite sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel * Power V + Punch II + Flame I + Infinity enchanted bow * Elytra (Unbreaking III + Mending) * 7 stacks of cobblestone, water bucket, 64 golden apples, 64 torches, 64 arrows, 64 fireworks, 64 cooked beef Success message: '''Given boss kit to N players!''' ====== bar ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Player(s) || Whose Integrity boss bar to modify. |- | Show || Boolean || Whether to show the boss bar. |- | Value || Number (0-1) || Health value displayed on the boss bar, where 1 = 100%. Required even when hiding the bar. |} Controls the Integrity boss bar. ====== jim_bar ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Player(s) || Whose Fractured boss bar to modify. |- | Show || Boolean || Whether to show the boss bar. |- | Value || Number (0-1) || Health value displayed on the boss bar, where 1 = 100%. Required even when hiding the bar. |- | Glow || Boolean || Whether the center of the bar glows. Required even when hiding the bar. |} Controls the [[Fractured]] boss bar with an extra glow toggle for the center animation. ===== chunk ===== ====== remove ====== Removes the entire chunk the player is standing on. Success message: '''Successfully cleared the chunk at (X, Z)''' ===== code ===== Commands related to the Corrupted Command Block. ====== get ====== Returns the current code for the Corrupted Command Block (read from MapVariables.code). ====== reroll ====== Resets the code to a fresh random string of 6-12 characters (StringExt.nextString(random, length, ...)). ====== status ====== Prints whether the code has been applied (MapVariables.codeApplied). ===== coord ===== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Where || clanvoid / maze / wood / stone / day_A || Which part of the void to get the polaroid coordinate from. |} Returns the X and Z coordinate of the Polaroid in the specified location of [[Clan Void]]. The returned coordinates are chunk centers, computed as floorDiv(coord, 16) * 16 + 8. * /tbs dev coord clanvoid → Wooden floor polaroid of Clan Void * /tbs dev coord maze → Maze floor * /tbs dev coord wood → Wooden floor * /tbs dev coord stone → Stone floor * /tbs dev coord day_A → Day A dimension ===== entity ===== Circuit-related commands to inhabit and discard creatures. ====== inhabit ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Entity || The entity to inhabit. |} Sets the CircuitInhabited flag on the targeted entity to true, allowing Circuit to possess it. The success message uses CMD_INHABIT_SUCCESS lang key. ====== discard ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Entity || The entity to discard. |} Forcefully removes the targeted entity or entities from the world (non-player entities only). Useful for entities that are immune to the normal /kill damage type. Implemented in brokencore. ===== event ===== Various event-related commands (from brokencore). ====== all ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Who || Player(s) || Players to trigger all events on. |} Runs every single registered event on the targeted players. Good luck! ====== debug ====== ====== story_time ====== Prints all scripted events part of progression. Requires the '''Event Debug''' config in BrokenCore to be enabled. The scripted events include: MoonCorruptionStoryEvent, TXTStoryEvent, NullBookStoryEvent, CoordsStoryEvent. ====== force ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Event || Event asset || The event to execute. |} Forces the specified event to execute. ====== random ====== Triggers a random event using the same system as the event scheduler. ====== schedule ====== Prints various information regarding events, including: * How many events are registered * How many events the engine executes per in-game day * Whether events are enabled globally * Pre-scheduled upcoming events (pending slots) ====== reschedule ====== (Dev environments only) Clears all schedules and regenerates them on the next tick. ===== fx ===== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Effect || Effect name || Which effect to toggle. |- | State || off / on / toggle || Sets the current state of the effect. |} Toggle the current state of any effect, useful for disabling stuck/long effects or testing them out. Available effects (organized by lang key): * aberration — Aberration (player) * vhs — VHS (player) * moon_glitch — Moon Glitch (player) * text_glitch — Text Glitch (player, special set [value] with float 0.0-0.0) * custom_sky — Custom Sky Color (player + special set [r] [g] [b] with integer 0-255) * sky_blue — Force Sky Blue (player) * screen_dupe — Screen Duplication (player) * lucid_blocks_effect — Lucid Blocks Pixelization (player) * meta_paranoia — Meta Paranoia (player) * glitches — Glitches (player) * void_box — Stage 2 Arena Border (player) * dream — Dream Effect (player) * invert — Invert Effect (player) Each player FX subcommand has toggle / on / off options (except text_glitch which uses set [value]). Only custom_sky exposes an extra set [r] [g] [b]. ===== give ===== ====== legacy_book ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | ID || String || The book's registration ID (looked up via BookLoader.getBook(id)). |} Gives the executing player a legacy book. '''Note''': The ID parameter is a string, not an integer. ====== library_book ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | ID || Integer (1-250) || The book's page number. |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Gives the targeted players a library book with the LIBRARY_BOOK_NUM DataComponent. ===== inspect ===== ====== tasks ====== ====== server ====== Prints the number of tasks queued on the server along with each task's class name and remaining delay tick. ===== jim_arena ===== ====== start ====== Starts the [[Fractured]] boss fight at the player's current location. Success message: '''Have fun...''' ====== create ====== Creates a new JimArena and adds the current player to the participants list. ====== destroy ====== Resets and destroys the JimArena. ===== overlay ===== ====== funny ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Plays the vine_boom sound and shows the flipper.png screen overlay for 15 ticks. ====== show ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |- | Texture || Image asset || The texture to display. |- | Duration || Integer || How long (in ticks) to display the overlay. Minimum 1. |} Shows any texture as a full-screen overlay to the targeted players. ====== clear ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Clears all active overlays from the targeted players. ====== silly ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Shows the integatlas.png screen overlay for 15 ticks. ===== player ===== ====== credits ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |} Sends the TBS end credits to the targeted players (via OpenCreditsPacket). ====== list ====== Lists all currently online players, excluding [[Null]]. ====== rep ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |- | Amount || Integer || The amount of reputation to give. Can be negative. |} Gives the targeted players an arbitrary amount of reputation. ====== send ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Players to teleport. |- | Dimension || Dimension asset || The target dimension. |} Teleports the targeted players to the specified dimension. ====== var ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Player || Player || Which player to query. |- | Variable || Any field name of PlayerVariables || Which variable to read. |} Reads any field of PlayerVariables via Java reflection. Useful for inspecting state variables like ban status, FOV, spawn position, etc. Field names are auto-completed. ===== popup ===== ====== show ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Recipients. |- | Title || String || The popup's title. |- | Message || String || The popup's body. |} Shows an arbitrary popup to the targeted players (via OpenAlertPopupPacket). '''Please use this responsibly.''' ===== reputation ===== ====== add ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Amount || Integer || How much reputation to add. |} Behaves the same as /tbs dev player rep @s <Amount>. Must be executed by a player. ===== set ===== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Type || moon_phase / null / spawn || What core variable to modify. |- | Value || Depends on Type || Self explanatory. |} Modifies some core variables: * moon_phase → MapVariables.moonStage (integer 0-2) * null → null joined (flags Null as joined, broadcasts the join chat message and sound) or null gone (flags Null as gone) * spawn → sets the player's spawnPos to the block they are standing on ===== structure ===== ====== set ====== ====== null_id ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Pos || Coordinates || Position of a null_structure block. |- | ID || String || The structure ID (e.g. aftermath / watching / wrong_tree / blackout / fate). |} Sets the structureId of the NullStructureBlockEntity at the given position. Fails with "Not a Null Structure Block. Maybe try setting the coords right?" if the block at Pos is not a null_structure. ===== summon ===== ====== fake_player ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | User || String || The username to impersonate. |} Spawns a [[Circuit#Deceiver|Circuit (Deceiver)]] next to the player with the specified user's skin. The user's UUID is resolved via UserAPI.lookupUuid(user); the selected player and custom name are set 10 ticks later. ===== time ===== ====== set ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Time || DAY / MIDNIGHT / NIGHT / NOON || Preset time of day. |} Sets the real time of day via TimeOfDay.set(level), similar to vanilla's /time set. ====== fake ====== ====== set ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Time || Integer (0-24000) || Time in ticks. 6000 = NOON, 18000 = MIDNIGHT. |} Sets a more precise fake time. ====== fake [time] ====== Sets the fake time using a TimeOfDay enum value. ====== fake off ====== Disables the fake time, reverting to the real time. ===== update_capes ===== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Players || Player(s) || Targeted players. |} Force-refreshes the capes of the targeted players. Success message: '''Forced cape update for N players!''' ===== world ===== ====== carve ====== Starts a ChunkCarver at the player's current chunk to dig a hole, filling the empty space with Barrier blocks. Success message: '''Carving hole at [X, Z]...''' ====== corrupt ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Where || Coordinates || The center of the corruption. |- | Radius || Integer || The circular radius of the corruption. |} Corrupts a circular region of the world around ''Where'' with the given ''Radius'' (via TerrainCorrupter.corruptTerrain). Success message: '''Successfully corrupted terrain!''' ====== resetSeed ====== Resets the world generator's internal seed (via SeedSwapper.swapSeed). Unrelated to the [https://minecraft.wiki/World_seed World seed]. ====== var ====== {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Name || String || Variable name. |} Reads any field of MapVariables via Kotlin reflection. ====== gametime ====== (Dev environments only) {| class="wikitable" ! Name !! Values/Type !! Description |- | Tick || Integer || The new server game time. |} Directly sets the server's game time. {{Wiki_navbox}}

pages.title: Concrete
pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}} {{Distinguish|text= [[Items#Concrete|Concrete]], a block with the same name}} [[File:Concrete 1.png|thumb|The Concrete dimension.]] '''Concrete''' is a nightmare dimension, accessible through sleeping. == Mechanics == === Ambience === As long as the Player is in the dimension, '''concrete.ogg''' will play. [[File:Concrete.ogg]] === Fall Damage === All fall damage is negated in '''Concrete'''. === Peaceful === No entities will naturally spawn in '''Concrete'''. == Overview == '''Concrete''' consists three endless lines of stacked 16x10x9 hallways made of a block of the same name, with a line of water at the middle of each hallway. These hallways start at Y = -54, and stretch up to Y = 243. In between each line, there is nothing but the void. Additionally, nothing else generates outside of these three lines. There is a sun in '''Concrete''', although this sun seems to be more akin to the vanilla sun than the one found in the Overworld. == Exit == Dying within '''Concrete''' will send the Player back into the Overworld. Additionally, jumping into the Void will result in the same. == Gallery == Concrete 2.png|Between the Concrete. Concrete 3.png|Above the Concrete. Concrete Endless.png|Endless Concrete. Concrete Sun.png|Concrete's Sun texture. Concrete Teaser.png|Concrete from the 2.0 Gameplay Teaser == Notes == * There is some similarity of endless hallways between both '''Concrete''' and [[Null Torture]].
{{Wiki navbox}} [[Category:Dimensions]] [[Category:Nightmares]]

pages.title: Curved
pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}} {{Distinguish|text = [[DyeXD412]], a Player}} {{Entity infobox |title=Curved |image= {{GalleryHelper |Curved-wiki.png¦Transformed¦Transformed Curved |Curved-decoy-wiki.png¦Decoy¦Player Form |CurvedWiki.png¦Pre-2.0 Design }} |Nicknames=DyeXD412 |Type=[[Entities#Souls|Soul]] |Association= [[DyeXD412]] |HP=125 |Armor=5 }} '''Curved''' is a player-like [[Entities|entity]], formerly a player named [[DyeXD412]]; in appearance his body appears to have been parasitized by void entities. He is notably one of the very few entities that can take damage and even be killed by normal Minecraft weaponry, though this may be because DyeXD412's actual body has not been completely transformed/parasitized. == Spawn == Curved can spawn naturally in the Overworld. All of the following conditions must be satisfied: * '''Difficulty''': Not Peaceful * '''Biome''': Not Ancient City (unless triggered separately) * '''World state''': Null joined * '''Boss fight''': Does not spawn during [[Integrity|Integrity Boss Phase 1]] * '''Player distance''': No SURVIVAL player within 158 blocks * '''Player position''': Player and Curved must share the same cave/surface context (both underground or both above ground) * '''Probability''': Approximately 1 in 2857 * '''Superflat penalty''': In a superflat world, the already-low chance is further multiplied by 0.1% * '''Cooldown''': After a successful spawn, sets 40000 ticks (≈33 minutes) before the next can occur '''Cave-surface-surface pairing''': When the player is in a cave, Curved spawns underground, and immediately enters its '''transformed form'''. When the player is on the surface, Curved spawns as a decoy, and waits to be triggered. === Special Summoning === Aside from natural spawning, there is another way to summon Curved: '''Clan Build structure summoning'''. While within 100 blocks of a [[Structures#Clan_Build_Overhaul|Clan Build Overhaul]] structure, the Player can say one of two triggers: {{tooltip|Not_It_Cal|Capitalization is ignored, spaces are treated as _.}} or {{tooltip|Disc_13|Capitalization is ignored, spaces are treated as _.}}. Null must have joined the game at this point. After {{tooltip|5 seconds|100 ticks}}, Curved will appear in his decoy form in a random direction 50–100 blocks from the Player. What it does afterwards is covered above. Additionally, when Curved spawns, a message in chat from [[DyeXD412]] will be sent, responding based off of the trigger used to summon him: ''"Somewhere, I'll find you."'' for [[Not_It_Cal]] or ''"I'm listening. I'm trying."'' for Disc 13. [[File:Aftermath-curved.png|thumb|none|Successful special spawn]] [[File:Clanbuildoverhaul-isorender.png|thumb|none|The structure]] '''This method can only work once every structure.''' == Stats == * '''Maximum Health''': 125 * '''Movement Speed''': 0.35 * '''Follow Range''': 916 blocks * '''Attack Damage''': 7 * '''Armor''': 5 * '''Knockback Resistance / Knockback''': 5 / 1 * '''Step Height''': 2.6 blocks == Appearance == === Decoy form === When disguised, Curved takes on a normal default Steve skin with its head tilted slightly to the side. === Transformed form === When transformed, Curved’s body darkens and mutates as his face turns pitch-black. A tentacle resembling a void entity is present emerging from the right shoulder, with additional tentacles present in the left ribs and the occiput. After the mutation, Curved's torso curls back into a hunched posture, its right hand props the ground, while three tentacles prop the ground like spider legs, with the other three limbs suspended in mid-air. == Behaviour == === Decoy === Curved can spawn on the surface of the Overworld, as well as in caves. Upon spawning, Curved is in its Decoy form, typically standing still. In Decoy form, Curved will slowly approach the player with a limping gait when it isn't being directly observed, only standing still if it's being looked at. Curved.gif|Idle animation before transformation Curved-normal-walk.gif|Walk animation before transformation === Transform === [[File:Curved-transform.gif|thumb|The transformation]] When Curved is close enough to a player, it will mutate, accompanied by curved_transform.ogg'''curved_transform.ogg'''. Its body parts violently tremble, the upper-left of its head cracks open first, the body bends backwards, then a tentacle resembling a void entity emerges from the right shoulder, followed by additional tentacles from the left ribs and the occiput. During this process, the contrast of its skin gradually increases and its face turns pitch-black. After the mutation, Curved's torso curls back into a hunched posture, its right hand props the ground, while three tentacles prop the ground like spider legs, with the other three limbs suspended in mid-air. === Pursuit === After the mutation completes, Curved immediately launches a fierce attack on the player, destroying blocks in its path and stamping the ground loudly. Curved can switch between crawling / chasing / swimming based on the surrounding terrain. During this period, it can take damage from the player. === Voice Lines === If a wall or similar obstruction sits between Curved and the player such that Curved cannot see the player, and the player is moving at that moment, Curved will say the following lines in a weak, hysterical voice: * '''''Hello?''''' * '''''Who is there?''''' * '''''Who are you?''''' * '''''What did you do?''''' * '''''I hear you.''''' (It sounds like "see" here, but the in-game subtitle reads "hear".) * '''''Is that you?''''' === Death === When Curved is killed, it roars in great pain as its body dragged underground by a black yarn-like mass. Killing Curved drops all of DyeXD412's belongings and displays: DyeXD412 left the game [[File:CurvedLeavingAfterDeath.png|thumb|RIP]] A list of drops: * 1-25 Cobblestone * 1-25 Iron Ingots * Diamond * Dirt * [[Items#Music Disc 16|Disc 16]] * Oak Log * Oak Planks * Oak Sapling * Redstone Torch * Rotten Flesh * Stone Sword * Stone Pickaxe * String * [[Items#Torn Paper|Torn Paper]] [[File:Curved-loot-EN.png|border|300px|A list of drops, displayed by the mod Loot Journal|none]] == Notes == * The image and name of the old Curved were most likely inspired by [https://minecraftcreepypasta.fandom.com/wiki/Curved this creepypasta of the same name], though aside from the name and the hunched posture, the two seem to share little resemblance. * Curved's new design is intended to look like "a Circuit" is puppeting his body, according to the modeller. This was inspired by Circuit's pre-2.0 behaviors, where it had a chance turn into Curved.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yrmjWnym6AQ ** It's not directly confirmed as to what void creature(s) is controlling Curved, but it's heavily implied to be [[Circuit]] as the black limbs are similar to that of Circuit. This is further reinforced since Curved used to be one of the results of a Mineshaft Circuit encounter aswell as Circuit being able to shapeshift == Gallery == |-|Gallery= Bad_posture.jpg|Menu fanart Caveboy.jpg|Menu fanart |-|Animations= Curved-idle.gif|Idle Curved-chase.gif|Chase Curved-crawl.gif|Crawl Curved-crawl2c.gif|Switches from crawl to chase Curved-c2crawl.gif|Switches from chase to crawl Curved-hurt.gif|Hurt Curved-swim.gif|Swim Curved-swing.gif|Swing Curved-death.gif|death animation |-|Sounds= '''The Voice of Curved''' by Zetos {{#evu:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Gn3c5AVa70&feature=youtu.be}} Voice Lines {{Clear}} [[File:curved_notice1.ogg]] [[File:curved_notice2.ogg]] [[File:curved_notice3.ogg]] [[File:curved_notice4.ogg]] [[File:curved_notice5.ogg]] [[File:curved_notice6.ogg]] Hurt {{Clear}} [[File:curved_hurt.ogg]] Footsteps {{Clear}} [[File:curved_step_1.ogg]] [[File:curved_step_2.ogg]] [[File:curved_step_3.ogg]] [[File:curved_step_4.ogg]] [[File:curved_step_5.ogg]] Death {{Clear}} [[File:curved_death.ogg]] [[Category:Entities]]
