pages.title: Cut and unused content
pages.extract:
{{Stub|Missing events, sounds, screens and images}} {{Version|1.10.1}} The Broken Script has gone through many changes over time. While some updates added content such as events, entities, or structures, previously added content can also be removed. Some of these removed features can still be found in the files, or by exploring older versions. Added content can also sometimes be unused, only being visible by exploring the files of the mod itself. = Cut content = Cut content can be things that were removed completely, things that were removed but were then added back, or things that were not removed but that ended up changing. == v0.71 == v0.71 is the oldest version of The Broken Script that can be found in the archives page. Most of the content found in this version is now scrapped or has been changed. Most hostile entities will make black vertical lines (Glitch frames) appear on the screen, and entities could spawn in any dimension. === Entities === ==== Error 1 ==== Error 1 was an spawnable entity in The Broken Script. From what we can see from its model and texture, it used to be a grayscale cylinder shaped entity. Decompiling some of the procedures, such as the Tick Update procedures shows us that this entity could spawn Null Chase, play sounds like a rumbling sound or a jumpscare sound. File:Error1.png|Error 1 in Blockbench File:Error1 in game.gif|'''Error 1 in game''' ==== Error 2 ==== An old version of what appears to be [[Hetzer]], named "Error 2", was an spawnable entity in The Broken Script. His model appears to be a cube with 3 vertical rings and 3 horizontal rings. File:Error2.png|Error 2 in blockbench File:Error2 in game.gif|'''Error 2 in game''' ==== Error 3 ==== An old version of [[Integrity]], named "Error 3", was an hostile entity that is very different from the modern Integrity. Instead of being a 9 blocks tall void entity, it was shorter, and much more similar to TBOTV's Integrity. His behavior was also different: * His watching behavior seems to be unspawnable. * His chase (Execute) behavior will randomly change the time to day or night. He is also able to break block, especially when he takes damage or gets punched by the player. When that happens, the blocks below him will break. Integrity was re-added in Spectrum 11. File:Error3.png|Integrity in 0.71 File:TBOTVIntegrity.png|An encounter between Integrity and players in TBOTV Act I ==== Error 4 ==== An old version of [[Sub Anomaly 1]] named "Error 4", was a common hostile entity that only looks different from the current Sub Anomaly 1. Instead of using black squares as particles, Sub Anomaly 1 would use the eyes particle. It also had a name tag above it displaying the word "Obstruction". Just like the current Sub Anomaly 1, anything that gets close to it gets damaged. The only difference here is that Sub Anomaly 1 would also damage itself. Sub Anomaly 1 was re-added in 1.9.1. File:Eyesanomaly.png|Sub Anomaly 1 in 0.71 File:Obstruction.png|Sub Anomaly 1's name tag ==== Error 5 ==== An old version of [[r2]], named "Error 5" was a common hostile entity that uses the same texture as the current r2. His behavior was a little different. R2 would always follow the player, like one of his current behaviors. The other behavior where he'd just stand around is not present. R2 would often turn into null chase instead of using his own chase behavior R2 could also turn into Error 5 (Execute), just like Error 3. This behavior is similar to his current chase behavior. ==== Null ==== Null, unlike his current version, was much more hostile. Null would have a watching behavior, just like he does right now. Approaching this version of Null would turn him into [[Null#Chase|his chase]]. In some cases though, the player would be teleported to the Nether. His chase behavior is still used in the current version of TBS. Instead of being named null_chase, it's now nulll. In his chase behavior, Null could be damaged (He has 700 don't try to fight him). Null Scare was already present too, as Null Jumpscare. ==== Is Player Hidden ==== The Broken Script often uses entities to check the position and behavior of players, or other things. In 0.71, the mod used an entity to check if the player was hidden. === Blocks and items === ==== Err 3 Block ==== Err 3 Block is a block with an animated static texture that will crash the game when it's broken. File:Err3Block.png ==== Disruption ==== The disruption block was dropped by Null when he died. This version of Disruption was named "Block", and the player could not walk through it. It also does not despawn. Instead, it would spread and create large cubes that would keep growing. ==== name.null ==== name.null was named "Item". Right clicking it in this version does not make it disappear. ==== Null 0 ==== Null 0 is a broken music disc that, when inserted into a jukebox, would play the music "The universe - Null". ==== Null Tp Beacon Spawn Egg ==== This item is a spawn egg automatically generated by MCreator. It was never meant to be obtainable in any way. You can find it in the Spawn Eggs tab in Creative mode. === Events === ==== Blick ==== Blick is an event where the screen randomly turns black for less than a second. This event can happen randomly, but it is also forced when some of the hostile entities are attacking the player. ==== Fire ==== Fire would randomly appear on the player. ==== HERE I AM GUI ==== A GUI that would say "HERE I AM" could randomly appear. ==== null.err GUI ==== A GUI that would say "null.err" on the top could randomly appear. [[File:Null.err GUI.png|frameless]] ==== Random Texts ==== Some texts might appear in chat box randomly. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |+Random Texts !Texts !Translation/Notes |- |outside. | |- |присоединился к игре |joined the game |- | |(whitespace) |- |Leave. | |- |Here I am. | |- |01010010 01100101 01101010 01101111 01101001 01100011 01100101 00101110 |Rejoice. |- |It. | |- |We know. | |- |Avoid it at all cost. | |- |The object. | |- |The broken scripts and codes. | |- |Found you. | |- |Null | |- |Can't be removed. | |- |They are no longer with us. | |- |It came from the void. | |- |Hello. | |- |Err1 | |- |Err2 | |- |Err3 | |- |Err0 | |- |Followed. |''whispers to you:Followed'' |} [[File:Random texts.png|none|thumb|'''Random text''']] ==== Random Items ==== Give the player random items. ==== Use main hand item ==== If the main hand is holding an item, it will be randomly used automatically. === Structures === Every structure that were present in TBS 0.71 were removed in 0.8. ==== Brick house ==== The brick house is a common structure that can spawn right when the world is created. It often appears along with the NULL cobble structure and the glass pillar structure. [[File:The brick house,glass pillar and NULL cobble structure.png|none|thumb|The brick house,glass pillar and NULL cobble structure]] ==== Glass Pillar ==== A tall glass pillar structure that is pretty common. It's taller than the current glass pillar structure. [[File:The tall glass pillar in v0.71.png|none|thumb|The glass pillar]] ==== Null Cobblestone Text ==== A common structure that can spawn is "NULL" written in cobblestone. [[File:NULL cobblestone text.png|none|thumb|NULL cobblestone text]] On the right side of the structure is a sign that reads "null null null null". [[File:The sign.png|none|thumb|the sign]] ==== Random Structures ==== Multiple random structures can spawn. They seemingly make no sense. The random structures that can spawn are: * A cobblestone cross on the ground. * Multiple larger cobblestone crosses supported by a cobblestone pillar. * Redstone with brick blocks on top of it. * Water in the ground * A 3x3 brick cube with a redstone block inside. === Advancements === There were only two advancements in 0.71. ==== Here I am. ==== This Here I am advancement used to not have any item or block as its icon. The description for it was "Null. Null. Null." [[File:Here I am advancement v0.71.png|none|thumb|Here I am advancement v0.71]] ==== Null Null Null ==== The Null Null Null advancement had a different background. There were also spaces between the "null"s. [[File:Null Null Null advancement v0.71.png|none|thumb|Null Null Null advancement v0.71]] === Screens and images === ==== Glitch Frame ==== Vertical black lines that appear when the player is getting chased by a hostile entity. [[File:Glitch Frame.png|none|thumb|Glitch Frame]] ==== White noise ==== White noise that has 4 frames. ==== Void creature ==== A blurry image of what may be Error 3 can be found in the files. [[File:Snimok ekrana 2024-08-28 144251.png|frameless]] === Moon Phase === The 5th moon phase of original Minecraft game will be replaced by a broken moon texture. [[File:Moon Phase v0.71.png|frameless]] === Main Title Screen === ==== Splashes ==== The text flashing on the main title of v0.71 is relatively monotonous compared to now, with the text almost all showing as 'Null'. There is a small chance of it appearing as 'I'm here', 'Help.', and 'Please.', as if someone is calling for help from the player. [[File:Splash"Null".png|frameless]] [[File:Splash"I'm here".png|frameless]] == v0.8 == === Entities === ==== Notexture ==== Notexture's behavior was exactly like 0.71 r2's behavior. It has a chase behavior but getting close to him had a higher chance to spawn null. === Blocks and items === ==== 431434 ==== The 431434 block used to have a different texture named "nullvoid". The player could walk through it as if it didn't exist, and the block did not do anything. [[File:431434 block v0.8.png|none|thumb|431434 block v0.8]] ==== 404block ==== This block is now named ""£!&!"*$)$"!*("_!)"($!" ==== Jumposcorooo spawn egg ==== Just like Null TP Beacon's spawn egg, this item not supposed to exist. === Events === ==== Broken Moon screen ==== This event was extremely common, happening every few seconds. An image of the broken moon's eighth phase would appear and cover the screen. That same image is used when the player gets too close to faraway, except that it's way more distorted now. [[File:Broken Moon screen v0.8.png|none|thumb|Broken Moon screen v0.8]] === Moon Phases === Be added in v0.8 and removed after v1.9 versions. Unlike the current version as a random event, it directly modifies the original moon phases in Minecraft. [[File:Moon Phase Old1.png|frameless]] [[File:Moon Phase Old2.png|frameless]] [[File:Moon Phase Old3.png|frameless]] [[File:Moon Phase Old4.png|frameless]] === Screens === ==== Eye ==== A semi transparent eye texture would appear often when the player triggered one of many chase behaviors. == v0.9 == === Blocks === ==== Empty ==== When an empty block is placed, it explodes after 25 seconds. Now, this block explodes instantly when it's placed [[File:Empty block v0.9.png|none|thumb|Empty block v0.9]] == v1.0 == === Dimensions === ==== Null Torture ==== In this version, [[Null Torture]] used to be infinitely generating bedrock rooms. In 1.9, Null Torture became a series of infinitely generating bedrock hallways. [[File:Null Torture.png|none|thumb|Null Torture v1.0]] == v1.1 == === Entities === ==== Cave Nickname ==== Cave Nickname was an invisible entity that would spawn in caves. It had the username "WHYERS4". Cave Nickname was the only instance of [[WHYER4]] as an entity (with a different username too). He was added in 1.1 and removed in 1.4. [[File:Cave nickname.png|none|thumb|cave nickname]] ==== Hetzer ==== While not being implemented in game directly, [[Hetzer]] already had a model and a texture. His model was similar to Error 2's model. He was a cube with 3 rings around him. His texture was a simple dark gray fading to black. [[File:Hetzer v1.1.png|none|thumb|Hetzer v1.1]] ==== The Broken End ==== The Broken End in 1.1, despite being hostile, was one of the least dangerous entities. He would only be slightly faster than the player, and would deal almost no damage. [[File:The Broken End v1.1.png|none|thumb|'''The Broken End v1.1''']] ==== The Obliteration ==== The Obliteration's model was already present in 1.1. ==== Ticktest ==== Ticktest was an entity with the texture of [[Hetzer]]. It was removed in 1.8. It's one of the multiple check and test entities of TBS. In v1.1, Ticktest is a neutral entity that deals 1.5 hearts at a time. [[File:Ticktest v1.1.png|none|thumb|Ticktest v1.1]] [[File:Ticktest.png|none|thumb|Ticktest entity v1.8]] === Blocks === ==== False Command Block ==== This block had the texture of a command block except that it did nothing. === Screens === [[File:Readable BSOD screen.png|none|thumb|Readable BSOD screen]] The BSOD screen's text was readable. == v1.2 == v1.2's archive file is broken and therefore cannot be played. == v1.3 == === Entities === v1.3 had a file named "ENTITIES INFO" hidden in the assets. This file reveals that Faraway and Nothingiswatching's names used to be "White Null" and "Censorship". [[File:ENTITIES INFO.png|none|thumb|'''ENTITIES INFO''']] ==== Revuxor ==== In v1.3, [[Revuxor]] was a hostile entity that would attack the player like null instead of banning them. Revuxor had 3 different behaviors: * His "Stare" behavior would just look at the player and walk slowly towards him while his model switched between random, incoherent poses. He would also become invisible for a few seconds. * His "Ceiling" behavior would spawn excessively in other dimensions. Revuxor would walk on the ceiling. * Getting close to Revuxor Stare or Revuxor Ceiling would trigger his chase behavior. He'd run extremely quickly. Many {{particle_icon|revuxor_particle}}particles would spawn around him and the player's camera would look in random directions. His chase theme was revuxor_chase.ogg'''revuxor_chase.ogg'''. [[File:Revuxor chase.png|none|thumb|Revuxor chase]] ''"Entity 5 - Revuxor'' ''Entity type - Observer'' ''Appearance - Glowing black and white steve'' ''Behavior - Kinda similar to null, but it's chase form is way more dangerous. He will chase you longer, he is faster than null, and can break EVERY block, ignores boats, can swim in water, will switch player's gamemode to survival. also player's screen will glitch a bit."'' File:Revuxor1.3.png|Revuxor Stare in v1.3 ==== Circuit ==== While this behavior does not seem to be present in game, Circuit used to have a 30% chance to trigger a minigame. The sound now entitled integrity_speech_and_counting_1.ogg'''integrity_speech_and_counting_1.ogg''' would play, and the player had about a minute to go back to the surface. ''"Entity 4 - Circuit'' ''Entity type - Attacker'' ''Appearance - Tall 2d entity with rhombus head'' ''Behavior - Circuit will spawn ONLY in the caves bellow level 30, it will sometimes watch player and despawn when player gets too close, or sometimes will stalk player and when it gets close enough it will jumpscare player and start it's chase, in it's chase form it can break blocks randomly. If you will look at him, with 30% chance minigame can start, where circuit will start counting to 60 seconds, and you need to get out of the cave before time runs out. If time will run out... Well.. You are cooked."'' === Blocks and items === ==== Flesh ==== Flesh was a block that was only present in 1.3. It is unknown how this block would spawn in the world.It disappears after being placed for 10 seconds, and there will be a sticky sound effect both when placed and when it disappears. [[File:Flesh.png|none|thumb|Flesh]] ==== Noise ==== Noise was a white noise block that could only spawn in the noise fractal structure. Due to it getting removed in v1.4, spawning noise fractal now does nothing. [[File:Noise.png|none|thumb|Noise]] ==== Unstable Noise ==== Unstable Noise was an animated white noise block that could only spawn in the noise fractal structure. Due to it getting removed in v1.4, spawning noise fractal now does nothing. [[File:Unstable Noise.gif|frameless]] ==== Redrock ==== Redrock was a brown bedrock-like block. Its texture is now used for the Clanbuild Anomaly Generator. [[File:Redblock.png|none|thumb|Redblock]] ==== Record 1 ==== Record 1 was a disc that had the same texture as 13. It played a reversed message when it was inserted in a jukebox.
"My ears are bleeding, my eyes are gone, our bodies are torn apart because of one bastard. Is this fair?"
[[File:Playing Record1.png|none|thumb|'''Playing Record 1''']] Apart from "My ears are bleeding", these exact words can be found on the reversed text signs in [[WORLD2]]: * "Is this fair?" is found at spawn, at the bottom of the broken chunk. * "My eyes are gone", "Our bodies are torn apart" and "All because of one bastard" can be found in a tunnel with many redstone torches. == v1.4 == === Entities === ==== The Obliteration ==== In 1.4, the Obliteration was added a WIP. It was supposed to ban the player from their world. A distorted sound is played before crashing the game and making the world unplayable. The Obliteration was officially readded in 2.0 [[File:The Obliteration v1.4.png|none|thumb|The Obliteration v1.4]] Confirmed by the original author wendigodrip, The Obliteration plays no part in the lore. [[File:Wendigodrip confirm obli nolore.png|none|thumb]] The design of this entity directly references content from [https://minecraftcreepypasta.fandom.com/wiki/Beta_1.2_02 Beta_1.2_02]. [[File:Wendigodrip confirm obli.jpg|none|thumb]] === Dimensions === ==== Clan Void ==== Clan Void before 1.9 was an infinitely generating cobblestone maze similar to the backrooms instead of rooms with their own purpose. [[File:Clan void before v1.9.png|none|thumb|clan void before v1.9]] == v1.5 == === Entities === ==== The Broken End ==== The Broken End became more dangerous. His texture also changed, making his eye smaller. He also had multiple red eyes when he became angry. [[File:TBE v1.5.png|none|thumb|The Broken End v1.5]] ==== Void ==== Void is an unspawnable entity. It is unknown what it does. == v1.9 == ==== Unfinished Integrity Boss Fight (1.9-1.9.7) ==== This was an older iteration of Integrity's boss fight that was originally planned for the 1.9 update. Although the first phase was completed, the boss fight was seemingly scrapped after most of the TBS community voted against it in a poll made by wendigodrip on the first official Discord Server. This version of the fight could only be spawned using commands, and its first phase was completely removed in version 1.10.1. The boss fight was eventually revisited and completed in the released 2.0 update, although the fight differs significantly from this early 1.9 iteration. The mechanics described below therefore only apply to this older, unfinished version of the fight and should not be taken as a description of Integrity's final 2.0 boss fight. In this early phase 1, Integrity would emit static noises, while eerie ambience, created by constantly playing random cave/eerie sounds at different pitches, would originate from his location. Integrity would slowly approach the player and can destroy any blocks in his way. He seemingly would not lose aggro on the player. He would randomly use the following abilities: '''Missiles:''' Integrity would summon several black, wirey missiles from the sky, which would explode upon impact. '''Status Effects:''' Integrity would inflict the player with Blindness and Slowness. '''Invisibility:''' Integrity would turn invisible and move significantly faster, making his movement appear almost like teleportation. Upon activating this ability, he would also play a voice line. '''Error Blocks:''' Integrity would summon Disruption blocks (similar to [[Notexture]]) at random positions around himself. '''Increased Event Rates?:''' Event rates appeared to increase while Integrity was active, although this was never confirmed. == v.2.0 == === Blocks === ==== Console ==== The Console was an indestructible block. Interacting with it pulls up a GUI with 4 buttons and a text field for entering prompts. As of version 1.9, this block has only one which is to teleport the player to the Overworld from any other dimension by entering the "sv.exit" command. Entering certain names will overwrite the entered prompt with a message. {| class="wikitable" |+Console Block Responses !Input !Response |- |"null" |"Outside" |- |"xXram2dieXx" |"Error" |- |"Integrity" |"ERR.NEXTNIGHT" |} [[File:CONSOLEGUI.png|thumb|left|GUI of the Console block|241x241px]]
=== Dimensions === ==== Day B ==== '''Day B''' was an infinitely generating set of rooms made of protected void blocks. The rooms are three blocks tall, and the floor and ceiling are two blocks thick. Lights are unevenly placed, making it dark in some areas- although the only mobs that spawn are Maze Shadows that spawn on the dirt of the dimension and not directly in the rooms. File:VoidExp6_2.png|The small console room, as seen from not too far away. File:VoidExp6_1.png|The same room but closer to the player. File:Dayb_consoles.png|Once again the same room, but inside. ==== Day A ==== The dimension known as '''Day A''' was changed to be the top layer of [[Clan Void]]. The actual content of the area was mostly the same. = Unused content = Unused content is stuff that is in the mod but is not used anywhere. It can be things that do not appear naturally, unobtainable items or content only found in the files. == In game == === Blocks and items === ==== OUTSIDE ==== OUTSIDE is a white block that acts like honey blocks when you walk on it. ==== Instability discs ==== While Instability V2 is craftable, the other discs do not seem to be obtainable for now. ==== Breads ==== Circuit Bread and Null Bread are unobtainable. === Advancements === ==== You've brought it upon yourself. ==== This advancement can only be obtained through the /advancement command. It uses name.revuxor as its icon, and its description is "It was your fault.". [[File:You've brought it upon yourself advancement.png|none|thumb|You've brought it upon yourself advancement]] === Structures === ==== Memory1 ==== Memory1 is an older version of the Clan Build structure. It appears to not spawn at all. ==== Noise Fractal ==== Noise Fractal was a structure that could appear when the noise blocks were still in the game(v1.3). Since these blocks are gone, spawning the structure does nothing. [[File:Noise Fractal.png|none|thumb|Noise Fractal]] === Particles === ==== Wretched particles ==== These particles were used for an old Revuxor chase behavior. === Sounds === == In the mod's files == === Blocks === ==== Block4 ==== Block4 is a black block with red dots. It can be seen in TBOTV in mbDelta for example. ===Entities=== ==== Anomaly1 ==== An unspawnable entity featuring a texture similar to [[R2#He|He]]. Anomaly.png|Anomaly1's texture. Anomaly1infiles.jpg|Anomaly1's model found in the files Wendigodrip once stated that [[Sub Anomaly 1]] would have a “scary friend” in version 2.0. Given the strong name similarity between Anomaly 1 and Sub Anomaly 1, there was a theory that this entity would be the "friend" and would debut in 2.0. However, instead of Anomaly1, [[Sub Anomaly 2]] would be added into 2.0. [[File:Scary friend.jpg|none|thumb|scary friend]]

== v1.9.9-beta (Extracted from the SMP pack) == === Subjugate === [[File:SubjugateWIP.jpg|thumb]] Subjugate is a pitch-black entity whose limbs are woven from void tendrils, possessed of extreme aggression and malice. In version '''''thebrokenscript-1.9.9-beta.1 mc1.21.1''''', it appears as an unfinished mob that cannot spawn naturally.
[[File:thebrokenscript-1_9_9-beta_1 mc1_21_1.png]] Like other Void creatures, its tall frame is latticed with ebony tendrils; yet whereas they terminate in triangular heads, Subjugate's head is rather elongated. ==== Appearance ==== Once summoned, its head snaps and contorts in grotesque, wide-angle jerks while its limbs quiver ceaselessly. It sprints and scales terrain with inhuman velocity, closing the gap in heartbeats and erasing the player in a single blow. ==== Behavior ==== The moment it materializes, it begins to speak subjugate_minigame.ogg'''subjugate_minigame.ogg''' — an audio originally slated for both [[Circuit]] and [[Integrity]], yet never given to either. ==== Audio ==== subjugate_chase.ogg'''subjugate_chase.ogg''' subjugate_living.ogg'''subjugate_living.ogg''' subjugate_minigame.ogg'''subjugate_minigame.ogg'''\ === Disruptor === A pitch-black entity whose limbs are composed of entwined tendrils, elusive and seemingly non-aggressive. ==== Appearance ==== [[File:DisruptorWIPingame.png|thumb|300px|Disruptor|none]] Unlike other Void entities, '''Disruptor'''’s body, though likewise constructed from tendril-like black strands, appears as if melted; its head is somehow a little bulbous rather than completely triangular, resembling a duck’s; its lower limbs dissolve into a spreading puddle of black tendrils. ==== Behavior ==== Disruptor’s head and upper limbs tremble faintly from side to side. Should a player approach within three blocks or look directly at its head, the Disruptor vanishes instantly to a faint despawn sound of disruptor_despawn.ogg.mp3'''disruptor_despawn.ogg'''. Many other unused assets can be found in the files of 1.9.9. This is because Subjugate and Disruptor at the time were supposed to be added to public TBS releases, and that they originally come from a fanmade addition mod. The assets that can be found in 1.9.9 come from a very early dev version of that mod and most of them can be ignored. == v1.10 == === In the mod's files === ==== disruptor_egg.png [[File:Disruptor egg.png]] ==== Though '''Disruptor''' and '''Subjugate''' do not exist in this version, Disruptor's spawn egg's texture still exists. ==== Missingno spawn egg.png [[File:Missingno spawn egg.png]] ==== A spawn egg texture for a currently unknown entity. ==== Error 3 ==== Even though Error 3 has been removed a long time ago, his model and an updated texture can be found in the files. While this could be just a leftover from the scrapped assets added in 1.9.9, it's odd that these two stayed. [[File:Thedesintegratorv2.png|none|thumb|Error 3 in v1.10 file]] == Former cut content == Content that was reintroduced in a later update === GUI === ==== Inventory Corruption ==== There are multiple corrupted inventory textures in the files which may be used for an inventory corruption event or mechanic. This was added in 2.0 Inventorycorrupted1.png|Inventorycorrupted1.png Inventorycorrupted2.webp|Inventorycorrupted2.png Inventorycorrupted3.webp|Inventorycorrupted3.png Inventorycorrupted5.webp|Inventorycorrupted5.png Inventorycorrupted6.webp|Inventorycorrupted6.png ==== Main Menu Splashes ==== The splash text display the player's username was introduced originally in v0.71, but was readded in 2.0 [[File:Splash"Player's name".png|frameless]] === Entities === ==== The Obliteration ==== In 1.4, the Obliteration was added a WIP. It was supposed to ban the player from their world. A distorted sound is played before crashing the game and making the world unplayable. The Obliteration was officially readded in 2.0 [[File:The Obliteration v1.4.png|none|thumb|The Obliteration v1.4]] Confirmed by the original author wendigodrip, The Obliteration played no part in the lore, though with its inclusion in 2.0, this is likely untrue [[File:Wendigodrip confirm obli nolore.png|none|thumb]] The design of this entity directly references content from [https://minecraftcreepypasta.fandom.com/wiki/Beta_1.2_02 Beta_1.2_02]. [[File:Wendigodrip confirm obli.jpg|none|thumb]] ==== Phantom Player ==== Phantom Player is a biped entity with a white noise texture. It does not move, and is not affected by gravity. It also has the username "__blackout__" and is killable. In the current version 1.10 he seems to could spawn naturally, and will become a [[Hetzer]] some time after spawning. He usually seems to spawn at places that coordinates y=100. It was readded in 2.0. [[File:Meet blackout .png|none|thumb]] ==== Null Unbeatable Bossfight ==== Null has an Unbeatable Bossfight that appears to not spawn naturally. When killed, he'll drop a field generator block. He has a white boss bar, his name is [] and he can only be killed through commands. It was readded in 2.0. {{Wiki navbox}}

pages.extract:
{{Version|1.10.1|specific}}
{{Distinguish|text = [[Day A]], the top layer in [[Clan Void]]}}
[[File:Day A.png|thumb|300px|Day A]]

'''Day A''' is a dimension consisting of two layers, for the sake of simplicity here referred to as '''Day A''' and '''Under Day A'''

Entering '''Day A''' can be done by chance when the Player is within 10 blocks of [[Notexture]].

== Mechanics ==
=== Ambience ===
As long as the Player is in the dimension, '''null dimension ambient.ogg''' will play.

[[File:null_dimension_ambient.ogg]]

=== World Generation ===
'''Day A's''' world generation is an altered version of Minecraft's Overworld world generation.
* No natural features (Such as trees) or structures generate within the dimension
* Water is replaced with quartz blocks
* All stone variants have been replaced with chiseled stone bricks.
* All grass variants have been replaced with dirt.
<gallery>
Day A Dimension Overworld.png|Overworld map
Day A Dimension UnderDayA.png|Day A map
</gallery>

== Day A ==
Day A itself is resembling a superflat world, featuring short grass and oak trees. It is possible to find terrain that generated higher than the fields generate as well.

The field is composed of only 1 layer of grass blocks, and a layer of bedrock beneath it, sitting the Player around Y level 97.

This plain will continuously generate so long as a '''Field Generator''' is loaded. If one is not loaded, then '''Under Day A''' will be uncovered completely.

== Under Day A ==
[[File:Under Day A.png|thumb|300px]]
The lower layer is full-fledged terrain, similar to that of the Overworld. 

If a portion of Day A has already been loaded, and the Player is transported to a different location within the dimension, they can experience the dimension without the problems of darkness above their heads.

{{Clear}}

== Gallery ==
<gallery>
Day A Dimension Layered.png|The divide between the layers.
Day A Dimension Endless Quartz.png|Endless Quartz.
</gallery>

== Notes ==
* The Day A dimension has since been removed after the ''2.0 Update'', and has been integrated into a layer of the [[Clan Void]] instead.

[[Category:Dimensions]]
{{Wiki navbox}}

pages.title: Day B
pages.extract:
{{Version|1.10.x|specific}}

'''Day B''' is an infinitely generating set of rooms made of protected void blocks. The rooms are three blocks tall, and the floor and ceiling are two blocks thick. Lights are unevenly placed, making it dark in some areas- although the only mobs that spawn are [[Maze Shadow]]s that spawn on the dirt of the dimension and not directly in the rooms.

In certain rooms, it is possible to find purple console blocks that can be interacted with via text prompts. While some commands that can be typed in have some silly effects, the console block can be used to get out by using "sv.exit".

Entering Day B can be done by jumping into the void and reaching y = -80. Keep in mind though that it does not always work. If you have access to commands, teleporting you to -80 has more chances of sending you to it than jumping into the void, since the player needs to be at EXACTLY y = -80. 

In 1.10+, entering Day B can be done by simply  jumping into the void and no longer requires you to reach exactly y=-80. 

When approaching [[Null]] during its Watch behavior, there is also a 10% chance of being teleported to the DayB.  

It was removed in 2.0 in favor of [[Protected Void]].  <gallery>
File:DayB Entering.png|What a player can see when entering Day B (even before the rooms start generating.)
</gallery>


Day B has 13 rooms. 8 of them are labeled as VoidExp 1-11 (With VoidExp 4, 5 and 10 missing), VoidExp edge, VoidExp edge passage, VoidExp Console Room, Void Hallway and Void Hallway Exit.

Even if this is another dimension, events can still happen.<gallery>
File:DayBWater.png|Water.
</gallery>

== Rooms ==

=== Large Room ===
Labeled as VoidExp 1, this room is a large room with no unique structures inside, often splitting into small hallways that lead to one of the other two room types. Lights are unevenly placed, leading to some areas being dark.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp1.png|Large open room.
</gallery>

=== Large Room with a wall 1 ===
Labeled as VoidExp 2, this is a less open room that also generates frequently. It has 3 openings and a wall. When in contact with VoidExp 1, it can generate huge open hallways that contrast with the claustrophobic atmosphere of the place.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp2.png|Another large open room but with a wall.
File:VoidExpLargeRooms.png|An example of rooms connecting, creating larger rooms.
</gallery>

=== Large Room with a wall 2 ===
Labeled as VoidExp 3, this is the same room as VoidExp 2 but rotated.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp3.png|Yet another large open room with a wall (but rotated!)
</gallery>

=== Small Console Room ===
Labeled as VoidExp 6, this is a small room blocked by protected void doors, containing 3 consoles on pedestals. There is a single void light in the ceiling, in one of the corners.

The consoles aren't any different from the typical console block, and don't yield any different responses.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp6 2.png|The small console room, as seen from not too far away.
File:VoidExp6 1.png|The same room but closer to the player.
File:Dayb consoles.png|Once again the same room, but inside.
</gallery>

=== Hallways room ===
Labeled as VoidExp 7, this room generates multiple hallways that the player can go through.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp7 1.png|The hallways room, seen from a certain side.
File:VoidExp7 2.png|Another side of that room.
File:VoidExp7 3.png|Or maybe it's THESE rooms?!
File:VoidExp7 4.png|Who knows?
</gallery>

=== Cross Room ===
Labeled as VoidExp 8, this room, which is not really a room, generates 2 walls in a diagonal cross that can separate several rooms. It can often connect to itself to create closed rooms.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp8.png|One side of the cross.
File:VoidExp8Closed.png|2 sides connecting created a closed and inaccessible room.
</gallery>

=== Pillar Room ===
Labeled as VoidExp 9, this room that usually connects empty rooms and small console rooms, full of pillars and narrow, one block paths between them. In the middle of this room there is a console on a pedestal, surrounded by a 2 block high wall with a one block wide entrance.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp9.png|The pillar room from outside.
File:Day b pillars.png|The inside of the pillar room.
</gallery>

=== Cross room 2 ===
[[Category:Dimensions]]
Labeled as VoidExp 11, this room also generates walls in a cross shape that can separate several rooms.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExp11.png
</gallery>


==Rooms（1.10＋）==

=== Edge ===
Labeled as VoidExp Edge, the edge seems to be a limitation to the VoidExp rooms. It comes as a giant block with no openings or hidden rooms inside.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExpEdge.png|An example of what the edge could look like.
</gallery>

=== Edge passage ===
Labeled as VoidExp Edge Passage, this is another version of the edge with 2 crossing hallways limited by protected void doors.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExpEdgePassage.png|An example of what the edge could look like.
File:VoidExpEdgePassage 2.png|The inside of the edge passage.
</gallery>

=== Console room ===
Labeled as VoidExp Console Room, this room is a large room with several pillars, several doors and one singular console in it.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExpConsoleRoom.png|An example of what the console room could look like in Day B.
</gallery>

== Unused rooms ==
The rooms do not generate through the VoidExp Generator block, meaning that they're either unused or scrapped.

=== Hallway ===
Labeled as Void Hallway, the hallway is a large room, with a higher ceiling than any of the other VoidExp rooms. In the past, Day B could've been what Null Torture is today.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExpHallway.png|An example of what the hallway could've looked like (it does NOT fit).
</gallery>

=== Hallway exit ===
Labeled as Void Hallway Exit, his is a version of the hallway room that generates a wall of exit blocks.<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:VoidExpHallwayExit.png|An example of what the hallway exit could look like.
</gallery>
== Floating Islands ==
Like other dimensions, DayB also possesses a lower stratum. Though the upper layer is impervious to pick or spade, one may descend by eating a chorus fruit. The lower stratum is a floating island wrought of bedrock and dirt blocks. It is worth noting that this isle appears to have been transmuted directly from The End.

<gallery widths="240" heights="240">
File:DayB 下.png|The lower stratum
File:DayB＆TheEnd Map.png|Comparation


</gallery>{{Wiki navbox}}

pages.extract:
{{Stub|reason=Missing section for Limbo, Lucid, and Moon. Not enough information on Library.}} {{Version|2.0.5}} '''Dimensions''' are additional dimensions added by the mod. Unlike those in vanilla Minecraft, a portal is not always necessary to enter them and entry can be unpredictable, with various entities and blocks being able to teleport the player to these dimensions. = List of Dimensions = == Nowhere == [[Nowhere|Main article: Nowhere]] Nowhere is a barren dimension containing many layers of 5-block high vine looking terrain made of mud, with the void being clearly visible. Falling into the void leads you to [[Dimensions#Protected Void|Protected Void]]. This dimension gets darker the further down you go. File:Nowhere_Dimension.png|The top layer of Nowhere, with a view on the bottom. File:Dimension_Nowhere_Structures.png|Various structures in Nowhere. == Clan Void == [[Clan Void|Main article: Clan Void]] Clan Void is a multi-layer dimension consisting of, from top to bottom: * '''Day A''': An endless superflat-like field with trees and grass, with structures scattered throughout. It is accessed via falling through the bottom of [[Dimensions#Nowhere|Nowhere]], walking through a [[Items#431434|431434]] block, or by falling to the bottom of Clan Void itself. * A dark, empty cobblestone ground. It is accessed by breaking the bedrock of the dimension above. * A large, wooden area with empty rooms containing bookshelves in the corner, and sometimes bridges. It is accessed by finding a hole in the ground in the dimension above. * A dark maze made with nothing but cobblestone, with occasional pyramids. It is accessed by finding a staircase in the dimension above. * A layer reassembling a house, containing an infinite set of cobblestone rooms, with a smooth stone sand, glass, torches. It contains many different types of rooms. It is the last layer, and can be accessed by finding a door in the dimension above. There is no terrain below Clan Void, leading to a void that puts you back to the top of the dimension when fallen through. Each layer also contains a piece of the [[Progression#Polaroid Pieces|Polaroid]], which can be found throughout each layer respectively. There is an entity resembling Null that can spawn that will chase you if spotted, and kill you with the message '''<player> was found.''' File:Day_A_2.0.png|Day A, the top-most layer. File:An Exit.png|An Exit File:Empty Room.png|Empty Room File:Stone Room.png|Stone Structure File:Crafting Room.png|Crafting Room File:Hub Room.png|Hub Room File:Storage Room.png|Storage Room File:Music Room.png|Music Room File:Furnace Room.png|Furnace Room == Null Torture == [[Null Torture|Main article: Null Torture]] Null Torture consists of very long 9x7 bedrock tunnels. On both sides of the tunnel are lava channels 2 blocks wide and 1 block deep. Whilst travelling through the dimension, it is possible to come across signs left on the floor by an unknown person, describing their stay there and thoughts. The tunnels have no intersections or a way out of them, so the player can only go forward or backward until they find an end. One end has a wall of blocks that function as the exit, while one end is a dead end and features a sign that reads "Wrong way", a chest with 27 music discs 11s, a jukebox, as well as four redstone torches. File:Exit POV of the Tunnels in Null Torture.png|Tunnels from the outside File:NullTortureWiki.png|Inside the Tunnels File:NullTortureExitWiki.png|An Exit File:NullTortureDeadEndWiki.png|An end of the Tunnels File:Null Torture Outside.png|Overhead shot of the outside of the Tunnels == Protected Void == [[Protected Void|Main article: Protected Void]] Protcted Void is a dimension containing nothing but a flight of stairs, and dors leading to small floors containing areas that look alike to Mark101's VoidExp. It is one of the few somewhat consistent ways to enter Clan Void before [[The Moon]] gets corrupted. Protected Void has two variants, the first variant is much more similar to VoidExp, whereas the second variant replicates content from The Broken Script itself. File:ProtectedVoidTop.png|Top view of the corridors in Protected Void File:ProtectedVoidEntrance.png|The [[Clan Void]] entrance, at the top-most floor File:ProtectedVoidExit.png|An exit, replacing the entrance after going through all floors File:ProtectedVoidVeins.png|A vein layer, found in variation one File:ProtectedVoidWindow.png|A window-like layer, found in variation one File:ProtectedVoidMoon.png|A black layer resembling the [[Moon]], found in variation two File:ProtectedVoidTorture.png|What seems to be a miniature [[Null Torture]], found in variation two File:ProtectedVoidClan.png|What seems to be a miniature [[Clan Void]], found in variation two == Mono Library (library) == [[Library|Main article: Library]] This dimension is accessible through sleeping in your bed, but has a low chance of teleporting you there, possibly acting like a "nightmare" It seems like a Infinite corridor, with Monochrome looking bookshelf blocks, which mining with a axe drops white books with cryptic text File:The_library.webp|The library. == Nothing == [[Nothing|Main article: Nothing]] Nothing is a dark dimension containing, true to its name, an endless flat layer. [[Nothing Watcher|Nothing Watchers]] spawn in this dimension, and the player is sent back shortly after. File:Nothing_Dimension.png|Nothing. == Limbo == [[Limbo|Main article: Limbo]] ''Stub. See main article.'' == Lucid == [[Lucid|Main article: Lucid]] ''Stub. See main article.'' == Moon == [[Moon|Main article: Moon]] ''Stub. See main article.'' [[Category:Dimensions]]

pages.extract:
{{Player infobox |title=DJ2trappy2skeezy |image= {{GalleryHelper |ForumDJ2.png¦Profile Picture¦Dominic |DJSkin.png¦Minecraft Skin¦DJ2trappy2skeezy |Dominic2008.png¦06/06/2008¦Dominic (primary school) |DominicDeceased.png¦Deceased¦Dominic (deceased) }} |Nicknames=Dom, DJ |Profile=[http://localhost:2018/profile/DJ2trappy2skeezy DJ2trappy2skeezy] |Died=2018 (aged 19) |Association=[[xoxDairyQueen]], [[RANKorous 123]], [[uImmortal_]] |Affiliations= Blacklisted }} DJ2strappy2skeezy, also known as Dominic, is a member of Blacklisted. According to their forum posts, he is [[RANKorous 123]]'s best friend. == Appearance == === Forum === === Minecraft skin === === 2008 === === Deceased === == Personality == Dom, just like most of Blacklisted, is immature and chaotic. He uses many emojis like [[RANKorous 123|Neb]]. While he doesn't explicitly show us his interests, he is a religious man. He is also very very close to [[RANKorous 123]], and losing her left him devastated. He pretends to be fine when he isn't. His relationship with her is ambiguous. On one hand she is described as his best friend by [[XoxDairyQueen]], and on the other hand he uses nicknames such as "babes". == Fate == === "Reunited." === Clicking on "i miss you." in the "yo" thread sends you to a google drive owned by [[XoxDairyQueen|Lucy]] with an image of Nebula and Dominic hugging in primary school. [[File:Reunion.gif|left|thumb|06 06 2008 - Nebula & Dominic - Primary School]]
The photo is actually a gif. There is one frame that, instead of having Neb and Dom as kids hugging, has them both dead, with Dom being ripped in half with his head also ripped off according to the lines on his body, while Neb seems to have gotten her chest pierced and possibly ripped open vertically too. [[File:ReunionDeadFrame.png|left|thumb|Reunited.]]
The cipher on the left of the photo gives us a link after a few corrections made by Dom, giving us more information about what happened to Dominic. http://localhost:2018/threads/DJ2trappy2skeezy/reunion
reunion 00/00/00 at 00:00:00 I thought I had lost her. Well, perhaps I still have. What remains of her truly holds no weight; only a stumbling congregation of shadow, gathered vaguely into the shape of what used to be her. At times, she turns towards me with something almost like recognition. Hollowed out eyes settled upon my face and for once merciful instant, I believe she is still there. That she knows me. Then her jaw hangs loose and the illusion rots. She is imprisoned within a carcass assembled all wrong. Every movement resembles a blasphemous imitation of life. Body twitching beneath ruined skin, each tremor a reminder that her body bestows a burial shroud filled with flies. Whatever found her must have been brutal. There is so little left that I recognise, save for the tufts of frizzy hair clinging stubbornly around her disfigured face. A tarnished ''halo''. I once thought I was a religious man. Truly, I did. I believed that there was intention behind suffering, that every wound was another line of scripture. But there is no scripture for this. What loving God would permit such a thing to kneel at the altar of His creation and feed? What divinity could watch something hollow her out, wear her likeness and drag her back to me like a cruel answer to a prayer. Maybe this is resurrection and we had misunderstood the promise. I think I am losing myself too. My thoughts no longer arrive in my own voice, something speaks for them. Something ravenous, deranged. It roots itself between my ribs, turning over each organ as if choosing from a banquet. '''My innards are it’s feast.''' '''My blood is it’s wine.''' '''My flesh is it’s bread.''' Yet, no communion is being held. Nothing is shared. Nothing is sanctified. It takes and takes, swallowing every sacred part of me without gratitude or reverence. Only greed. Incessant, fucking greed. ''I am not ready to forget her.'' I am not ready to lose her again. So, I remain before her and she before me. Two abandoned offerings at the foot of an empty altar, waiting for the other to remember what we once were. A melancholic reunion, or something cruel enough to resemble one.
It's possible that, after killing Nebula, Circuit wore her body and met up with Dominic to kill him too. == Forum presence == File:DominicForumProfile.png|DJ2trappy2skeezy's forum profile. pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5|major}} '''Entities''' within [[The Broken Script]] range from player-like to horrors of the Void made of strange, prehensile tendrils. Many of them are actively hostile while some are conditionally hostile dependent on player reaction to their presence (i.e. looking at them, attacking them, drawing too close to them, etc.). Abilities and behaviour can differ between entities, though the most severe outcome of an interaction with an entity from The Broken Script is the banning of the player from their own world. It is known that every ban instance in the main mod at the moment is an intervention by [[Revuxor]] in an attempt to save the player from the fate of other players. Entities, with the exception of the Void Creatures, were formerly players who were transformed by the Void Creatures either directly or indirectly. This can occur because of corruption, interaction with Void Creatures in-game, or by being killed in real life by a Void Creature. The effects of transformation into an Entity varies greatly between victims. Some Entities, like [[Null]], appear to have retained their consciousness, memory and ability to interact with the world and player. Others, like [[Hetzer]], are totally unrecognisable when compared to their previous selves and appear to be able to communicate with the Void Creatures in order to summon them. Why and how these differences exist is currently unknown, as is the transformation process. __FORCETOC__ == Souls == '''Souls''' are entities that were formerly human. Their capacity of intelligence and sapience is dependent on who they were, how they died, and where they died.
{{infocard |name=[[Null]] |text='''[[Null]]''' is a player-like entity and a splinter of 0nullvoid0's soul. Null will join the game (visible in chat) early into the play-through and will appear in the tab list. After he joins, he can start to appear in the player's world. Interactions with Null vary the most as he can be seemingly erratic, however it could be observed that Null is an entity that could be reasoned with. |image=Nullwatching.png }}{{Infocard|name=[[Faraway]]|text=Faraway will occasionally appear on the ground somewhere in the vicinity of the player and watch them. Occasionally they will slowly move towards the player if not directly looked at. Faraway is the only entity that doesn't try to kick, ban, crash, or otherwise harm the player. the only thing Faraway does is jumpscare you when you get to close to him, which after he dissapears|image=Faraway_in_the_wild.png}}{{Infocard|name=[[Curved|Curved]]|text=Listening to Disc 13 on loop corrupted him and over time turned him into an entity. He appears to be violently glitching, his model constantly shaking and visually teleporting around.|image=Curved-wiki.png}}
{{infocard |name=[[Hetzer]] |text='''[[Hetzer]]''' could be best described as a "spheroid" consisting of several rings encasing a small cube in the centre. It's texture seems to be white noise. Hetzer is an entity that seems to be shrouded in falsehoods, upon approach it will disappear and an edited version of Minecraft's calming Subwoofer Lullaby known as the False Subwoofer Lullaby will play before the music abruptly stops, time is set to midnight, and after a minute, [[Circuit]] will spawn. |image=Hetzer2.0.gif }} {{infocard |name=[[Notexture]] |text='''[[Notexture]]''' is a player-like entity with the ability to teleport the player to another dimension if physically interacted with. There's little information on him other than what is known of his behaviour. Notexture spawns and replaces blocks with missing texture blocks as it moves, it is seemingly hostile. |image=Follow2.0.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Nothingiswatching]] |text='''[[Nothingiswatching]]''' is a rectangular black censor box with nothing behind it. In some instances, its sprite will shake while idling or moving. Upon direct player observation black screen artifaction appears and Nothingiswatching will rapidly begin approaching the player, barrelling through physical objects damaging entities and destroying the blocks in its path. Getting hit by it causes the game to crash. |image=Nothingwatches.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Phantom Player|Phantom Player]] |text='''[[Phantom Player|Phantom Player]]''' is a player-like entity; formerly a player named [[Lore|Blackout]]. Upon spawning, Phantom Player will fly up in the sky and watch the player from afar; approaching it will make it despawn with a glitchy noise. |image=Phantom player.png }} {{infocard |name=[[r2]] |text='''[[r2]]''' is a deformed humanoid silhouette with no visible features. Approximately 3 blocks tall, and shakes erratically both when standing still and moving. Upon direct player observation r2 will either disappear or he will lock in on the player's location and rapidly begin approach. Physical contact with r2 will kill the player and crash their game. There appears to be no limit to how many r2s can spawn at a time. r2 can also make it where its unable to sleep, getting a err message when you attempt to sleep |image=Error5v2.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Revuxor]] |text='''[[Revuxor]]''' is a player-like entity with a monochrome Steve skin. One of the more mysterious player-like entities, as Revuxor, in any instance where the player is going to be banned, he appears behind them for just 1 tick. |image=Revuxor2.0.5.png }}
== Anomalies == This classification is for players who have been warped beyond recognition even more so than the Souls and Entities, or unclassified objects that only appear due to the void's presence. While most Anomalies are not as powerful as Entities, not outwardly hostile and appear relatively benign in their presence, a few have demonstrated considerably severe interactions with the player or their surroundings (such as the Obliteration) . Despite this some, like Sub-Anomaly 1, can still damage and kill the player. There are six (seven if counting Herobrine, eight if counting both obliterations as separate) known anomalies.
{{infocard |name=[[Herobrine]] |text='''[[Herobrine]]''' is a player-like entity with a darkened Steve skin and glowing white eyes. Yes, Herobrine from the creepypasta and legends seems to exist within the Broken Script. How he came to be, what his intentions are, and who his afilliations are with is unknown. |image=HerobrineWiki.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Maze Shadow]] |text='''[[Maze Shadow]]''' is a player-like entity that has pitch-black skin, reminiscent of [[Null]]. '''Maze Shadow''' is an enigmatic, evasive anomaly that seems to be able to exist anywhere, yet has no apparent purpose for its presence. It is unknown what Maze Shadow is or what its origins are. There is no limits to how many Maze Shadows can spawn at a time. |image=Maze shadow.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Nametag]] |text='''[[Nametag|Nametags]]''' appear as floating, playerless name tags, with a shadow cast beneath it and no visible body. The username shown is randomly generated. |image=Nametag.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Nothing Watcher]] |text='''[[Nothing Watcher|Nothing Watchers]]''' are floating pairs of red eyes. Upon spawning in, Nothing Watchers will simply stare at the player from afar, always facing them. Nothing Watchers don't seem to despawn when the player comes close, and the player can approach and even hit them without them despawning. |image=Nothing Watcher.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Sub Anomaly 1]] |text='''[[Sub Anomaly 1]]''' appears to be a "cloud" of black, spastic particles that has no discernible body or point of origin. Due to the appearance, it could be assumed this is a moving mass of corruption which will slowly move towards the player, inflicting damage when near. Not much can be said about it, since that is the only thing that it does. |image=SA1render.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Sub Anomaly 2]] |text='''[[Sub Anomaly 2]]''' is an anomaly that appears exclusively during the [[Fractured]] fight. Unlike its void-cloud predecessor, Sub Anomaly 2 features a spider-like structure of 7 corrupted limbs without a main body. |image=SubAnomaly2Render.png }} {{infocard |name=[[The Obliteration]] |text='''[[The Obliteration]]''' is a large, black star-shaped object. It can also be a large, black inverted pyramid with thin "ropes" beneath it. The Obliteration floats in the sky. If the player comes close to it, it can crash the game and/or kick the player from the world, and add temporary visual effects to the game. |image=Obliterations.png }} {{infocard |name=[[XXram2dieXX|xXram2dieXx]] |text='''[[XXram2dieXX|xXram2dieXx]]''' is a player-like entity and is likely a splinter of 0nullvoid0's soul. After breaking a hello block xXram2dieXx will have a chance of joining the world. The server will inform the player, "Local game hosted on port [2018]" and then a little while afterwards, xXram2dieXx will join the game and set the time to midnight. |image=XXram2dieXx.png }}
== Void Creatures == The '''Void Creatures''' are an anomalous and exceptionally dangerous amorphous organic species of extraterrestrial origin found within The Broken Script. They represent one of the most severe threats documented in the game, with encounters frequently resulting in the death, disappearance, or otherwise irreversible alteration of the player. Their biology, exact origins, and the exact nature of their connection to the [[Void]] remain poorly understood. Each of them are characterized by having black tendril and wire-like bodies, geometric-shaped heads and many red eyes. [[The Broken Script]] features six of these Void Creatures. They are considered the highest level threat in The Broken Script as encounters with them often end in the player's demise one way or another. Through unknown means and under unknown conditions, Void Creatures are seemingly able to leave the confines of the game and the machine hosting it to enter the real world. At least one Void Creature, [[Circuit]], is confirmed to do this by crawling out of the computer's monitor. The only known goal of this activity is to kill the Human player and drag them into the game permanently.
{{infocard |name=[[Chord]] |text='''[[Chord|Chords]] are the split form of a collective entity known as 'Harmony', though the reasons for it being split during the events of the mod are unknown. ''' |image=Chord-yester7render.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Circuit]] |text='''[[Circuit]]''' is lowest in the Void Creature chain of command. He is capable of shapeshifting, in order to trick the player. [[Null]] Believes that everything was all his fault, presumably due to the fact that Circuit impersonated Null and caused the downfall of the clan server. Of the Void Creatures, Circuit's behaviours are the most documented, as he frequently haunts the every action of players in the Broken Script. He is also very loud. |image=Circuit2.0.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Fever]] |text='''[[Fever]] is a manipulator, luring players using various methods before she eventually kills them.''' |image=Fever2.0.5flight.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Fractured]] |text='''[[Fractured]] is a colossal void entity residing on the moon, seemingly there to protect what resides within.''' |image=Fractured.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Integrity]] |text='''[[Integrity]]''' is a Void Creature and the main antagonist of The Broken Script, ultimately responsible for everything that has occurred. Nearing the end of 2010, Integrity gained access to cracked copies of Minecraft and began stalking players in singleplayer worlds before banning them. |image=Integrity phase 1.png }} {{infocard |name=[[The Broken End]] |text='''[[The Broken End]]''' is a very dangerous Void Creature, his size is hulking and works for [[Integrity]]. The Broken End is a very powerful entity, capable of doing irreversible damage to players by killing them and taking their souls. The Broken End is also capable of causing minecraft.chatengine failure. The Broken End is but one of many entities that can make it where you cant sleep, getting a err.theendisnear when trying to sleep while he's present. |image=The broken end2.0.png }}
== Easter Egg == Easter Egg entities are entities that are not part of the mod's lore and cannot spawn naturally. They are usually references to other media and added for joke purposes. {{infocard |name=[[Jon]] |text='''[[Jon]]''' is a blocky-looking Roblox noob with a poorly drawn face. Jon walks around aimlessly, and occasionally says either "Hello!" or "Let's play Minecraft!". He can be killed, in which case he will leave the game. |image=Jon.png }} {{infocard |name=[[Murderfur]] |text=Murderfur resembles a bleeding cat standing on it's hind legs, with a cracked screen on it's face. |image=Murderfur.png }} [[Category:Entities]]

{{Version|1.10.1|specific}} {{Entity infobox |title=Entity Spawner |image=[[File:Random entity.png|300px]] |Nicknames=Random Entity Wandering soul |Role= |Type=Technical |Affiliations= |HP= }} '''Entity Spawner''' is a technical entity in the mod that serves as a placeholder for most other [[entities]], while also acting as a mechanic to control spawn rates and limit the number of entities present at once. As entity spawning was reworked in 2.0 it appears this entity is no longer used as its not present. == Appearance == Entity Spawner is a humanoid entity that possesses the same model as the player, however its body is all missing textures. == Behaviour == For all intents and purposes, the normal TBS playthrough is not supposed to contain an Entity Spawner. To put it simply, seeing an Entity Spawner walking around is a bug. They are extremely basic in their behavior. They will wander around aimlessly, sometimes in groups, completely passive to the player. They cannot be directly harmed by the player, by melee or distance attacks, but can be lured into the void or killed by a Warden. They can be angered by a firework arrow pointed at them, which will cause them to aggro on the player. The Entity Spawner can only spawn if the moon phase is not '''Waning Gibbous''', if the sky is visible above it, and if it passes a {{tooltip|5%|1 in 20}} chance check. Upon successful spawn, it will immediately be replaced by one of the following entities: * [[Null#Flying|Null - Flying]] * [[Null#Watching|Null - Watching]] * [[r2|r2 - Roaming]] * [[r2#Stare|r2 - Stare]] * [[Circuit#Deceiver|Circuit - Deceiver]] * [[Notexture]] * [[R2#He|Him]] * [[Faraway]] * [[Nothingiswatching]] * [[Circuit#Creeper_Circuit|Circuit - Creeper Circuit]] * [[Circuit#Pig_Circuit|Circuit - Pig Circuit]] * [[Hetzer]] * [[The Broken End|The Broken End - Stalk]] (If [[the Moon]] Corruption Stage is 2) [[Category:Entities]] [[Category:Mechanics]] == Notes == A good chunk of information on the '''behavior''' of Entity Spawner's are from Auromancy's TBS series, so special thanks to him.

{{Version|2.0.5}} {{Entity infobox |title=Faraway |image=[[File:Faraway in the wild.png|300px]] |Nicknames= |Role= |Type=[[Entities#Souls|Soul]] |Affiliations= |HP= }} Little is known about '''Faraway''', as it cannot be closely observed and its origins are unknown. What is known about Faraway is that it is one of the few entities that doesn't try to kick, ban, crash, or otherwise harm the Player. Even when it is present, it doesn't prevent them from [[Err.sleep|sleeping]]. == Appearance == Faraway shares the same model as the Player, with a pure-white homogeneous skin that appears to glow. Faraway gives the impression of an ethereal presence, straddling the line between present and not present. Its model has an independent emissive render layer that gives it a faint supernatural sheen, even during the day. == Spawning == Faraway will only spawn if the sky is visible above it. Once spawned, it has a 70% chance to instantly despawn, which combined with its other restrictions makes actual encounters with it rare. Faraway additionally requires: * Null joined * No [[Integrity|Integrity Boss]] fight in progress * The player to be more than 65 blocks away from the spawn point * The world to not have spawned a Faraway in the previous 7 minutes 40 seconds (9200 ticks) * At most one Faraway exists in the world at any given time The base spawn chance is approximately 1 in 400, reduced to 1 in 1000 in superflat worlds. == Behaviour == Faraway will stay in place upon spawning, always facing and watching the Player. It will never attack, chase, or move towards the Player. If the Player looks directly at Faraway, regardless of it's distance, Faraway's "stare counter" will increase. Additionally, if the Player is within 38 blocks of Faraway and has a '''clear''' line of sight of Faraway within their FOV, Faraway's "stare counter" will increase. Once the "stare counter" is 25 or higher, accomplished by triggering either action above for 1.25 seconds, Faraway will [[#jumpscare|jumpscare]] the Player. If neither action occurs, the Player can approach Faraway as close as they would want. Faraway will despawn after {{tooltip|80 seconds|1600 ticks}}. === Jumpscare === When triggered, Faraway forces the Player's view toward itself and releases 555 particles ({{particle icon|null_particle}}null or {{particle icon|eyes}}eyes particles). The Player's screen is also covered for {{tooltip|0.75 seconds|15 ticks}} with a static-distorted image of the old 8th phase of [[the Moon]], accompanied by an audio cue. [[File:snimok_ekrana_2024-11-02_090828.png|border|300px|none]] === Funny Settings === If [[Funny Setting]]s are enabled, Faraway has two additional interactions, occurring at a 0.5% chance. * '''Baby''' — Faraway appears in a child-sized model. Audio and screen overlay use the very_serious/baby.png image. * '''Fard''' — Faraway emits 50 FARDAWAY_PARTICLE particles on despawn, with the very_serious/fardaway.png screen overlay. == Notes == * [[WORLD2]]'s '''icon.png''' [[File:WORLD2_icon.png]] (pre 2.0) and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bGW25bKHgiM Playing_alone.mov] are from Faraway's perspective. ** The implications and exact meaning of this are unknown at this time. * In earlier versions of the mod, Faraway was colloquially referred to as "White Null". * The item [[Items#Faraway Salmon|Faraway Salmon]] is based off of Faraway, findable in [[Clan Void#Wood|Clan Void]]. == Media == |-|Gallery= Faraway transparent.png|Transparent Faraway Render Farawayrendertbsfix.png|Artistic Render Baby.png|very_serious/baby.png Fardaway.png|very_serious/fardaway.png Theres_2_of_them.png|Two Faraways standing next to each other（pre-2.0） Faraway in map.png|Faraway displayed in the bottom left of Xaero's Map（pre-2.0） |-|Menu Fanart= John_far.jpg|Menu Fanart |-|Sounds= Disappears {{Clear}} [[File:phantom_disappear.ogg]] Funny {{Clear}} [[File:baby_disappear.ogg]] [[File:fardaway.ogg]]

{{Stub}} {{Version|2.0.5}} {{Entity infobox |title=Fever |image= {{GalleryHelper |Fever2.0.5flight.png¦Flight |Fever2.0.5walk.png¦Walk |Fever2.0.5root.png¦Root |Fever.png¦2.0.0~2.0.4 }} |Nicknames= |Role=Antagonist |Type=[[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] |Affiliations=[[Void]] }} {{Quote|text=The night sky is so beautiful, isn't it?|author=Fever's first quote to the player when they come to Limbo.}} Fever is an entity that can appear in various areas of the game, mainly [[Limbo]]. == Appearance == Fever is an 11 block tall mesmerizing entity with two pairs of wings, making her look like an angel. On these wings you can find vein like lines fading from red to a reddish pink, and multiple eyes with the same colors. Her ribcage is also slightly reddish. She has three arms. Two of them are regular arms while the third is like a hook attached to her left arm. On her back, there are two flower-like appendages, similar to the ones on [[Fractured]]'s. She also has red eyes similar to The Broken End's angry state, mostly red then fading to purple. The middle 6 possess faint white dots in them. If you look closer, another layer of dark red eyes intersects with the more visible ones. While she claims to be a savior, her head has multiple horns like a devil. == Personality == {{Quote | text = What a '''joke'''. To think that I thought that maybe, just maybe she would give me answers regarding my friends. A merciful deity with the answers at her disposal, yet, someone who wields a blade of silver. Ready to just gut me like the sickly pig I am. | author = [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 97 - 2/13|Dairy Queen]], frustrated about Fever's lack of answers for what happened to her friends. }} Fever is highly manipulative and usually plays more of the long-game with her victims by befriending them and acting as a companion. Most of her victims do not realize her true intentions or nature describing her as kind and skilled not realizing who they're dealing with. During one of her manipulations, Fever befriends a victim and demands their attention to the point of guilt-tripping them to stay with her. [[XoxDairyQueen|One of her victims]] describes her as a being of divine absurdity taking refuge and blames her for why "they never came back" though also seemingly goes insane as she claims to have awoken because of her. Unlike void entities, Fever is very open to conversations (even in game), interrogations, and does not mind getting recorded in books. She even at one point expressed disappointment of killing [[XoxDairyQueen]], claiming she took a liking to them. Despite this she is not afraid to show violence towards those who annoy her enough, those who ignore her, and those who would dare to abandon her no matter how much she can take a liking to them. Her claim of being a savior is either: * Fever trying to manipulate her victims to see her as a savior, making them follow any order or gaining their trust to kill them while maximizing despair as she seems to change her tactics depending on her target (becoming friends with [[Littleepic1|younger people]], becoming a "savior" for [[XoxDairyQueen|more mature people]]). * Fever genuinely seeing herself as a merciful savior and liberator that also is not afraid to kill anyone who angers her (she is very open to questions and interrogations, and [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 1: Fever|she will say nothing but the truth according to herself]].) == Spawn == === Limbo === She is guaranteed to spawn in [[Limbo]]. === Stalk === She can spawn naturally in the Overworld. All of the following conditions must be satisfied: * '''Difficulty''': Not Peaceful * '''Dimension''': Overworld only * '''Biome''': Any biome * '''World state''': Null joined * '''Boss fight''': Does not spawn during [[Integrity|Integrity Boss Phase 1]] * '''Sky exposure''': The spawn position must be exposed to the sky; it will not spawn under a roof or underground * '''Player distance''': A player must be within 512 blocks of the spawn position * '''Player position''': That (nearest) player must be at Y ≥ 130; the chance then scales with the player's height, up to a 75% ceiling * '''Uniqueness''': No other FeverStalk may exist within 512 blocks * '''Probability''': Depends on the current corrupted moon stage (see more at [[The Moon#Spawn Probability Matrix]]) * '''Superflat penalty''': In a superflat world, the chance is further multiplied by 0.1% == Behaviour == Fever behaves the same towards players regardless if they are in Survival and Creative modes. === Limbo === Fever will spawn immediately in [[Limbo#House|Limbo]]. Even if you discard her using commands, she will respawn once the dimension is exited and re-entered, or on re-logging the game. She will begin making their way towards the player, completely unaffected by player action until Fever is within 125 blocks of the Player. If within 125 blocks and looking at Fever, she will stop in place as static builds up on the Player's screen, filling it's way towards the center. Once it fills all the way, or if the Player looks away from Fever, she will continue flying towards the Player. Fever is also capable of loading chunks. By looking at a world map, the player can see that Fever's spawn chunk is immediately loaded. [[File:FeverSpawnChunks.png|left|thumb|400x400px|Fever's spawn chunks are already loaded (top left)]]
=== Fever Stalk === Fever will appear in the Overworld, and will begin tracking her way towards the Player, even through blocks. Fever is faster than a player flying in creative mode and she can fly through blocks. She will also slowly force the player to look at her while she's around. She only ever flies straight towards the player, but at two different speeds: * '''Stalk (calm)''': She flies towards the player at a slow speed. * '''Enraged''': If the player keeps her in view for 30 ticks (1.5 seconds), she becomes enraged permanently and flies at the player much faster, at a rate that Creative Flight is unable to escape. She will attacking on contact for 200 damage (enough to kill the player instantly). Looking away before that only resets her stare timer; once enraged she never calms down again. Whenever she hits the player, the player's screen is briefly inverted. If she reaches the player while calm (within 1.2 blocks), she disappears surrounded by eye particles, with an overlay that says "BE NOT AFRAID". If she kills the player, there is a 90% chance the player is kicked with the message "You are safe now." or "Do not be afraid.", and a 10% chance that she instead summons [[Ban]] at her position. The colors of the main menu will also be inverted. In Multiplayer, Fever will only target one player, doing the above behaviour for the targeted player alone. In addition, this player will be the '''only player able to see/hear Fever'''. === Death Messages === * When killed by Fever ([[Limbo]]): ** {USERNAME} never saw it coming. ** {USERNAME} didn't look behind them while fighting {MOB/PLAYER} * When killed by Fever Stalk (Overworld): ** {USERNAME} saw what they could not comprehend. ** {USERNAME} saw what they could not comprehend while fighting {MOB/PLAYER} == Additional Gimmicks == Fever's presence seems to cause weird effects, as [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 1 - 5/28|players in her vicinity are unable to fulfill any basic need such as eating, drinking or sleeping]], and they are also [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 27 - 43/57|not able to move from their PC]], [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 34 - 11/15|even after days]]. When she laughs, Fever does not have a single voice but [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 1 - 12/28|multiple overlapped and slightly de-synced voices]]. Fever's presence also seems to make people lose their sense of [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 21 - 50/50|time]]. Additionally, Fever seems to have the ability to [[XoxDairyQueen#Log 27 - 49/57|see people through their screen]]. == Dialogue == {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Prompt !Response |- |''Coming to [[Limbo]] for the first time.'' | The night sky is so beautiful, isn't it? |- |''Coming to [[Limbo]] for the second time.'' | We meet once again. |- |''Coming to [[Limbo]] for the third time and beyond.'' | ... |- |Where am I? | Isn't it much more intriguing to think about where you aren't? |- |What is this place? | This? This is a safe haven. You don't need to be afraid here. |- |What are you? | Don't fret, I am your Savior. |- |What do you want? | I want to see you, from the inside out. |- |Hello | Greetings. |- |The sky looks weird | Isn't it beautiful? |- |What are those houses? | Such flora, in the forest. |- |Fuck you, Asshole, Ass hole, Fucker, Piece of shit, Asshat, Fuck ass, Bitch, Bitch ass, Ass hat | That is no way to speak to your Savior. Do you wish for Judgement? |- |[[XoxDairyQueen|Lucy, xoxDairyQueen, DQ, Dairy_Queen]] | Her arrival was overdue. |- | | Do you have any feelings? |- | | Do you have a voice in your heart? |- | | Close your eyes and look at me. |- | | Be not afraid. |- | | The less visible something is, the more beautiful it becomes. |- | | Do you know who you are? |- | | Does this world bring you solace? |- | | What do you seek from here? |- | | Let yourselves be saved. |- | | Why do you look for the living among the dead? |- | | Do not be afraid, For you have found favor with God. |} == Notes == * Though Void Creatures canonically lack gender identities or a biological sex, Fever is referred to as she/her pronouns by her victims and the developers. * "Jacinthe" is a joke/placeholder name used for Fever during 2.0's development, as the developers didn't want to reveal its actual name. It has since become Fever's joke/alternate name in the community (as well as in the mod files). * It has been confirmed that Fever's design will not be updated further, however there are new mechanics coming. == Media == |-|Gallery= FeverLimbo.png|Fever at x:0 y:8 z:0 in Limbo.
