{{Infobox |title=spectrum_11.jar |image=New Spectrum11 Menu.png }} '''spectrum_11.jar''' is a secret secondary mod once found within the main mod's files prior to version 1.9 of The Broken Script, though a new version for 1.21.1 is available to download through a link [https://data.mc-anomaly-archive.org/files/spectrum_11.txt at the bottom of this page], and depicts events that chronologically happen before the events of The Broken Script. It takes place in Minecraft Alpha 1.1.2_01, many aspects of Minecraft 1.21.1 being altered or removed to mirror the version, though some like the off-hand slot or sweeping attacks are still present. Unusual things will happen to the worlds made in this version, including the complete alteration of the world itself. Eventually, an entity known as [[Integrity]] will appear in the world, which will eventually bring an end to the player, banning them from the world with a "Connection Lost" screen. [[File:Connection Lost v2.png|none|thumb|Connection lost]] ==Changes== * The game's appearance, including the menu, sounds and world generation, have been regressed to emulate the visuals of Minecraft Alpha 1.1.2. ** The menu now plays a custom theme, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYVlrYek7Og Arrival]. ** Trying to play the game with [https://modrinth.com/mod/iris Iris Shaders] results in a LWJGL pop-up saying ''"Trying to cheat the system, are we? Shaders did not exist in Alpha."''Taken from the mod's source code (spectrum_11-neoforge-0.0+mc1.21.1-build.8.jar), decompiled with Vineflower. The strings can be found at S11NeoClientEvents.kt, line 24 to 38. *** Additionally, trying to play the game with [https://modrinth.com/mod/distanthorizons Distant Horizons] will show a pop-up saying ''"Trying to cheat the system, are we? These horizons are quite close, after all."'' *** Attempting to use both Iris Shaders and Distant Horizons will show the same window, with the message ''"Trying to cheat the system, are we? There were no shaders and there were no farther rendering techniques."'' [[File:WeCan'tUseShaders.png|frameless]] * You cannot choose any other game mode other than Survival, nor can enable Cheats or change the world type through ''normal'' means. The difficulty is also locked to normal, even after world creation. [[File:OnlySurvival.png|frameless]] * The player's skin is forced to be Steve. Interestingly, in the files, this skin is labeled as "the first", suggesting that the Alpha player we take the role of is the first victim of Integrity. * The hunger bar is entirely absent, with food items directly healing the player. ** The latter no longer stack, including Rotten Flesh. * The armor bar is displayed where the hunger bar would be. [[File:No hunger bar.png|none|thumb|'''No hunger bar''']] * Sprinting is removed. * Punching Sheep also removes their wool. * Copper is absent, and Raw Iron & Gold have been redesigned to resemble their Ore block, similar to old Minecraft where you directly obtained the block to smelt it. * Grass and Tall Grass are entirely absent. ==Events== * "integrity.curious" - The player's render distance is reduced down to its minimum for a short while, with an eerie noise playing— it lasts an indeterminate amount of time. It plays the moonglitch.ogg'''moonglitch.ogg''' sound. * The sound of ~4-5 stone blocks being broken (displaying Block broken in Subtitles, if they are enabled). * Chunks being raised aboveground. This is also marked by sounds akin to cave sounds. [[File:Spectrum11 Raised Terrain.png|none|thumb|A portion of the world uprooted]] * "spectrum11:chunk_remover" - A chunk being erased entirely. Similarly to its The Broken Script counterpart, it is handled by an entity. * The player is displaced ~10 blocks behind their current position. * Minecraft's UI text suddenly becoming partially distorted. This becomes permanent, and will affect the menu aswell. [[File:Spectrum11 Text Glitch.gif|none|thumb|Text error]] * The player being kicked with the message "You still have some time." [[File:Spectrum11 Warning Kick.png|none|thumb|A warning.]] * "Here I am" and "Nowhere to run" LWJGL alert. [[File:Here I am LWJGL.png|frameless]][[File:Nowhere to run LWJGL.png|frameless]] ==Integrity Behavior== * Integrity will start to appear after a few days regardless of the player being above or underground. This is indicated by a bell resonating sound, and the version text becoming glitched when nearby. ** If not stared at, it will eventually despawn on its own after {{Tooltip|120 seconds|2400 ticks}}. [[File:Spectrum11 Glitched Version.gif|none|thumb|Glitched version display]][[File:Spectrum11 Integrity Bedrock Placement.png|none|thumb|Don't stare at it.]] * Staring at Integrity will cause one of 4 things to happen: ** The player will get kicked, with the error message ''"You still have some time."'' (20% chance) ** The player will get teleported to Integrity (20% chance) ** The player gets teleported to Integrity, and 40 blocks of Bedrock will be played around Integrity's position in a 10x10 block radius. (20% chance) ** Integrity will chase the player. (20% chance) ** Nothing happens. (20% chance) Do note that there is still a 50% chance for Integrity to chase you when despawning. * Integrity can split in half, playing a Integrity_split.ogggrotesque sound as it does. If this sound plays, Integrity has started to become aggressive, though it is possible for it not to attack. Once it decides to attack the player, usually on the last phase of the Moon, it will speak, declaring Youwillbecomeoneofus.ogg'''"You will become one of us"'''. It will teleport around in its pursuit to reach the player. While this happens, a s11_Integritychaseloop.oggunique theme plays on loop. ** Upon the player being killed, three LWJGL pop-ups will display before the player is banned permanently from their world. These can say "Beyond imagination" or "Nowhere to run" or "One of us." [[File:LWJGL pop-ups.png|none|thumb|LWJGL pop-ups]] == Moon Phases == Spectrum 11 alters all phases of the Moon, with the normal phases having hints of red off to their side that are barely visible. === Old Moon Phases === [[File:Spectrum11 Moon phases.png|none|thumb|'''Spectrum11 Moon phases (Old)''']] [[File:Spectrum11 moon phase1.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum11 moon phase2.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum11 moon phase3.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum11 moon phase4.png|frameless]] === New Moon Phases === [[File:Spectrum 11 Moonphases 1.21.1.png|none|thumb|Spectrum 11 Moonphases(v1.21.1)]][[File:Spectrum 11 MoonphasesNew 1.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum 11 MoonphasesNew 2.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum 11 MoonphasesNew 3.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum 11 MoonphasesNew 4.png|frameless]][[File:Spectrum 11 MoonphasesNew 5.png|frameless]] == Notes == * Events that alter the world may result in patches of black lighting in hollow spots. This is merely the result of the chunk not updating, and should be fixed by placing new blocks or torches. * Please, be careful while playing with older versions of '''spectrum_11.jar'''. The latest version (1.21.1) is not (as) invasive and does not open any powershell windows or interact with your system. * This mod does NOT contain any goofy "scary" faces. * When creating a world, Spectrum 11（1.21.1）will generate biome that replace the original Minecraft ones. Loading Spectrum 11 and entering a previously saved world may cause terrain glitches, so caution is advised. * In the description of the video for the track "Arrival", is where you can get the link for the text document that includes the mod's jar file. * The text document that includes the jar file gives some backstory on who wrote it, but it is in Russian. ** You can click [https://data-mc--anomaly--archive-org.translate.goog/files/spectrum_11.txt?_x_tr_sl=auto&_x_tr_tl=en&_x_tr_hl=en here] for a translated version of the text document. (Thanks to IPVOID) * After installing New Spectrum 11, players will not be able to complete Minecraft through the normal process, though we are able to go to Nether. When you get to the End by using cheats and beat the Ender Dragon, you will see the End Poem text was changed to "Your personal data has been compromised."（this is just there to scare you) * The original '''spectrum_11.jar''' is '''NOT''' present in files of 1.9.3 ver nor in other 1.9 versions currently. For now, you can find it in 1.8 version's files [see picture for the route]. ** If you don't have TBS 1.8, you can download it [https://www.mediafire.com/file/a83zt9h6vholf69/thebrokenscript-1.8-forge-1.20.1.jar/file here]. [[File:Spectrum 11 notes.png|thumb|Quick comparison of 1.8 and 1.9.3 versions' contents and the ''"Last warning"'' note in folder with '''spectrum_11.jar.'''|none]] ==Gallery== File:11title.webp|Old Menu screen File:Connection lost.png|Old 'Connection Lost' screen File:New s11 Integrity Transparent Render.png|New s11 Integrity Transparent Render [[Category:Lore]] [[Category:ARG]]

pages.title: Structures
pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}} Structures in '''The Broken Script''' are builds that randomly spawn around the world after some time. They will generate in loaded chunks within a range of the player, and can spawn within the player's view, usually indicated with an eerie or strange noise. These structures vary wildly and be as simple as a single block or as complex as whole bases. Some structures are benign, some are helpful, and some are designed to hurt or trick the player. Some structures contain [[431434|portal blocks]] that send the player to other [[dimensions]]. It is possible for structures to spawn in or on top of player builds, irreversibly replacing the original blocks affected. Destroyed chests will drop their contents. All random structure generation can be disabled in the mod's configuration file, as well as some individual structures. One of our community members has spent the time to document every single structure inside of TBS, which has been compiled into a video accessible [https://youtu.be/Y16vdetFVH8 here] (Outdated). = List of Structures = == Big Structures == === baserestored === A version of the old Clan Base from before it was destroyed by [[Blackout]]. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:baserestored [[File:baserestored.png|left|300px|thumb|baserestored]] {{Clear}} === baseruins === A version of the old Clan Base from after it was destroyed by [[Blackout]]. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:baseruins [[File:baseruins.png|left|300px|thumb|baseruins]] {{Clear}} === Carcas === Carcas is a frame of oak logs, featuring a chest hidden in the middle joint of the structure. The chest contains redstone dust, glowstone dust, and a book and quill. The book and quill reads: Why are you still there? Is there is something you are looking for? * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:carcas [[File:Carcas 1.png|left|300px|thumb|The Carcas Structure.]] File:Carcas 2.png|Chest inside Carcas Structure. File:Carcas 3.png|Contents of the chest inside Carcas Structure. File:Scary book.png|Book found within the Carcas structure. {{Clear}} === Cave Base Overhaul === [[Cave Base]] is another clan base belonging to [[Lore#Blackout's_Clan|Blackout's Clan]] that can spawn underground. Due to the underground nature of this structure and the way The Broken Script affects cave generation, a minimap mod or large-scale excavation is often required to find it. * The base has 8 rooms — 1 “clan rules” room, 3 rooms belonging to one of the players, 2 storage rooms, a Nether portal room, and a room containing a protected void block. * All other chests in the base are filled entirely with [[name.null]], except for one which contains a large amount of wood and glass. * A hidden sign which says "They are noting" with a redstone torch is behind the clan rules wall. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:cavebase_overhaul [[File:Cave Base.png|left|300px|thumb|Cave Base from above.]] File:Cavebase 1.png|Cave Base exposed in a cave. File:The secret sign behind the rules wall in Cave Base.png|The hidden sign behind the rules wall in Cave Base. {{Clear}} This structure takes over [[#Clan_Build_Overhaul|Clan Build (structure)]] when enabled, a '''50%''' chance. === Clan Build Overhaul === Main article: [[Clan Build]] [[Clan Build]] is a large 5-story build made of cobblestone and smooth stone. Signs found on each floor indicate that this base used to belong to [[Lore#0nullvoid0's_Clan|0nullvoid0's Clan]] before the Void Creatures began a campaign to kill or transform the Human players of the world. * The base contains chests filled entirely with missing texture items called name.null. They disappear from the inventory upon being used by the player, and otherwise serve little purpose. * Each floor has signs dated between 2018 and 2019, hinting at the [[Lore]] behind the base, and the Clan that lived in it. * The 5th floor of the base contains void blocks that will teleport the player to the [[Clan Void|clan_void]] when touched. They cannot be broken normally, but can be harvested with water and placed down elsewhere. All signs on this floor are dated '00.00.0000'. * The roof of the base has more signs and a circle of redstone torches that serve an unknown purpose. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:clanbuildoverhaul [[File:Clanbaseoverhaul 1.png|left|300px|thumb|Clan Base Overhaul front view.]] File:Clanbaseoverhaul 2.png|Clan Base Overhaul side view. File:Clanbaseoverhaul 3.png|Clan Base Overhaul top view. This structure takes over [[#Cave_Base|Cave Base (structure)]] when enabled, a '''50%''' chance. {{Clear}} === Mall === [[Not_It_Cal]]'s house from the Clan Server after her death, with some major damages. The music disc Mall can be found in one of the chests, as well as an assortment of [[R_3]], [[Vein]]s, and [[name.missing]]. * This structure can summon [[The Broken End#Ambush|The Broken End]] if [[Not_It_Cal]]'s name is written into chat. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:mall [[File:Mall_1.png|left|300px|thumb|Mall Front]] File:Mall_2.png|Mall Back File:Mall_3.png|Mall Inside {{Clear}} === Gorestructure === The Gore Structure is a small wooden build lit by redstone torches, and made entirely from oak logs and planks. Inside is a chest that contains 26 [[Items#name.revuxor|name.revuxor]] items and a book and quill which contains the following text: "01000100 01101111 01101110 00100111 01110100 00100000 01101100 01101001 01110011 01110100 01100101 01101110 00100000 01110100 01101111 00100000 01110100 01101000 01100101 01101101 00100000 00111101 00101001" This is binary, and when translated to ASCII characters reads: Don't listen to them =) * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:gorestructure [[File:GoreStructure.png|left|300px|thumb|The Gore Structure.]] File:Gorestructure 2.png|Hidden chest in Gorestructure. File:Gorestructure 3.png|Contents of the chest. {{Clear}} === Portal1 === A large cobblestone structure with a large opening that split into two parallel corridors. The right corridor ends in a wall of [[431434]]. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:portal1 [[File:Portal1 1.png|left|300px|thumb|Portal1 front view.]] File:Portal1 2.png|Portal1 middle corridor. File:Portal1 4.png|Portal1 right corridor. File:Portal1 3.png|Portal1 left corridor. {{Clear}} === Stoneaslym === 11x11x9 structure made out of 9 cobblestone rings. It has a single golden block in the middle of top and bottom layer with single redstone torch on top of both gold blocks. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:stoneaslym [[File:Stoneasylum 1.png|left|300px|thumb|Stoneaslym.]] File:Stoneasylum 2.png|Stoneaslym top view. {{Clear}} This structure takes over [[#Smallfractal|Smallfractal]] when enabled, a '''50%''' chance. == Small Structures == === 11 === A hopper pointed down into a jukebox, immediately playing disc 11. * Spawn Command: /place template thebrokenscript:11 [[File:structure11.png|left|300px|thumb|11]] {{Clear}} === 2bedrocks === 2 blocks of bedrock placed corner to corner with each other. * Spawn command: /place template thebrokenscript:2bedrocks [[File:Diagonalbedrock.png|left|300px|thumb|Self explanatory.]] {{Clear}} === afriendlost === A small wooden platform with 3 signs. pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}} {{Entity infobox |title=Sub Anomaly 1 |image=[[File:SA1render.png|300px]] |Nicknames= |Role= |Type=[[Entities#Anomalies|Anomaly]] |Affiliations= |HP= }} The origins of '''Sub Anomaly 1''' are unknown, but it is theorized that it is some kind of semi-sentient void corruption. == Appearance == '''Sub Anomaly 1''' appears to be a cloud of {{particle icon|null_particle}}null particles with no discernible body or point of origin. == Spawn == Sub Anomaly 1 can spawn naturally in the Overworld. All of the following conditions must be satisfied: * '''Difficulty''': Not Peaceful * '''Dimension''': Overworld only * '''Biome''': Any biome * '''World state''': Null joined * '''Boss fight''': Does not spawn during [[Integrity|Integrity Boss Phase 1]] * '''Sky exposure''': The spawn position must be exposed to the sky. It will not spawn underground or under a roof * '''Probability''': Depends on the current [[The Moon|moon phase]] (see table below) {| class="wikitable" ! [[Moon]] phase !! Spawn chance |- | 0 (Full Moon) || 0.1% (≈ 1 in 1000) |- | 1 (Waning Gibbous) || 0.5% (≈ 1 in 200) |- | 2 (Third Quarter) || 2% (≈ 1 in 50) |- | 3 (Waning Crescent) || 1.5% (≈ 1 in 67) |- | 4 (New Moon) || 1% (≈ 1 in 100) |- | 5, 6, 7 || 0% (cannot spawn) |} * '''Superflat penalty''': In a superflat world, the already-low chance is further multiplied by 0.1% * '''Uniqueness''': Only one Sub Anomaly 1 may exist at a time. It cannot spawn again until the current one is gone == Behavior == Sub Anomaly 1 will spawn on the surface and start wandering mindlessly at a very slow pace with the intent of approaching the player. Each tick Sub Anomaly 1 will deal 2 damage to every mob and player within a 2.5 block radius of its centre. Sub Anomaly 1 can replace blocks near it with Shadow Bug blocks that go back to the original block if you approach them. Sub Anomaly 1 can sometimes spawn a block named "Block Is Missing Id" around itself. It is also killable as of 2.0, having 50 health points. == Notes == # Even if you are within Sub Anomaly 1's radius, the damage can be stopped if a wall is between you and Sub Anomaly 1. # Initially, Sub Anomaly 1 was supposed to have a visible model, resembling a mix between a void creature and a spider. (The spider idea seems to be reused with [[Sub Anomaly 2]]) == Gallery == File:Image (2).webp|"Scrapped" model of Sub Anomaly 1. File:Sub Anomaly's HP.png|Sub Anomaly 1's huge HP value, visualized by [https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/wthit-forge WTHIT (What The Hell Is That)] (Pre-2.0) File:Sub Anomaly 1 Artistic render.png|Artistic render of Sub Anomaly 1. File:SA1render.png|New Sub Anomaly 1 render with Block is missing IDs around it. [[Category:Entities]]

pages.title: Sub Anomaly 2
pages.extract:
{{Entity infobox |title=Sub Anomaly 2 |image= {{GalleryHelper |SubAnomaly2Render.png¦Variant 1¦Transparent Render of Sub Anomaly 2 }} |Nicknames= |Role=Fractured Minion / Boss Anomaly |Type=[[Entities#Anomalies|Anomaly]] |Association= [[Entities#Fractured|Fractured]] |HP= |Armor= }} '''Sub Anomaly 2''' is an [[Entities#Anomalies|Anomaly]] that appears exclusively during the [[Fractured]] boss fight of 910 health. Unlike its [[Sub Anomaly 1|void-cloud predecessor]], Sub Anomaly 2 features a drastically altered physical structure consisting of corrupted, spider-like limbs without a main central body. == Appearance == Sub Anomaly 2 abandons the void-cloud structure of Sub Anomaly 1 in favor of an arachnid-like skeletal geometry composed of corrupted limbs: it lacks a traditional torso or main body, consisting instead of a central joint cluster from which 7 long, segmented legs extend. It does not have a single fixed appearance, but manifests as 7 distinct physical variants with unique textures. == Stats == * '''Health:''' 910 * '''Movement Speed:''' 0.33 (ground) / 0.85 (flying) * '''Step Height:''' 3 * '''Attack Damage:''' 1 * '''Follow Range:''' 40 * '''Fear Factor:''' defaults to 6 (initial light-avoidance threshold) * '''XP Reward:''' 0 * '''Properties:''' Cannot be pushed, cannot be leashed, fire-immune. == Behavior == === Spawning & Boss Encounter === Sub Anomaly 2 spawns during the boss encounter with [[Fractured]]. It is the main way of damaging the boss, with attack damage against the player intentionally set to 1 to make it a mechanic-focused mob rather than a damage threat. It auto-binds to the nearest [[Fractured]] within512 blocks. When [[Fractured]] dies or is defeated, Sub Anomaly 2 loses its target and disperses. === Light Avoidance === Sub Anomaly 2 fears light sources and will actively pathfind toward nearby ones (lava, torches, redstone torches, glowstone, etc.) and destroy them. Its behavior varies with light level relative to its current Fear Factor: * '''Light ≤ Fear Factor:''' at ease * '''Light > Fear Factor:''' seeks shelter Attacking it enrages it and raises its Fear Factor. If the Fear Factor reaches 12 or above, the light-avoidance mechanic is disabled entirely—Sub Anomaly 2 becomes insensitive to light.
In direct sunlight on a clear day (outside the [[Moon]] dimension), it despawns instantly. Shooting [[Fractured]] with a Flame enchanted bow, or Spectral arrows, turns Fractured into a light source, luring Sub Anomaly 2's into swarming it for damage. === Combat & Movement === Sub Anomaly 2 uses its 7 elongated legs to move quickly across the moon's surface, walking or flying toward the player to assist [[Fractured]] with 1 contact damage per hit. Flying speed (0.85) is significantly higher than ground speed (0.33), so once it enters chase mode it is very hard to outrun. The divebomb, however, is dodgeable: its dive direction locks at the moment of charge and cannot change mid-dive, so sidestepping the moment it hovers above you will make it crash into the ground. === Mimic (Currently Unused) === Sub Anomaly 2 includes an unused MIMIC (stealth) form: animation files exist (4 anims: MimicSpawn, MimicIdle, MimicTransformToSpider, SpiderTransformToMimic), but no code calls enter MIMIC state in the current version. == Gallery == Sa2-1.png|Variant 1 - Dark Red Tendril Sa2-2.png|Variant 2 - Black Limbs / Red Core Sa2-3.png|Variant 3 - Bright Crimson Tendril Sa2-2-4.png|Variant 4 - Fuchsia Checkerboard / Glitch Texture Sa2-5.png|Variant 5 - Cyan / Purple Gradient Sa2-6.png|Variant 6 Blue Limbs / Dark Fuchsia Core Sa2-7.png|Variant 7 Dark Fuchsia Tendril File:Image (2).webp|"Scrapped" model of Sub Anomaly 1. == Notes == # It is possible that Sub Anomaly 2's design is a revisited version of Sub Anomaly 1's scrapped early design, which was also spider-like. # Sub Anomaly 2 features 7 unique visual variants rather than a single static design. Variant 5 is the rarest. # Sub Anomaly 2 Does not spawn naturally due to it being unfinished because of 2.0 time constraints. [[Category:Entities]] [[Category:Anomalies]]

pages.extract:
{{Version|2.0.5}} {{Entity infobox |title=The Broken End |image= {{GalleryHelper |The broken end curious2.0.png¦Calm (2.0+)¦The Broken End (Calm) |TBEangry_w.png¦Angry (2.0+)¦The Broken End (Angry) }} |Nicknames= Administration |Role= |Type=[[Entities#Void Creatures|Void Creature]] |Affiliations=[[Void]] }}{{Quote | text = DO YOU KNOW HOW THIS HAPPENED? WE'LL TELL YOU THEN. WE DRAGGED THEIR INNOCENT SOULS HERE. FOR THEM IT ALL FELT REAL. THEY TRIED TO HIDE IN THE MINE. WE FELT THEIR FEAR THROUGH THE SCREEN. WE BLOCKED THEIR CONTROL OF THE MOVEMENT AND SLOWLY BEGAN TO MOVE CLOSER. TEARS FLOWED DOWN THEIR CHEEKS. BUT THEY COULD NOT EVEN CRY OUT IN PAIN. THE CHAT WAS ALREADY CORRUPTED. AND WE LEFT THIS TRAITOR FOR OUR LAST. HE SAW EVERYTHING WITH HIS OWN EYES. HE BEGGED US NOT TO HURT HIS FRIENDS. BUT IT WAS ALL OVER FOR THEM. AND EVENTUALLY, FOR HIM. | author = Scrapped The Broken End speech in the files. }} '''The Broken End''' is an intelligent and exceptionally dangerous Void Creature. It is known that he is lower in authority than [[Integrity]], and most likely carries out Integrity's orders, as he is called Administration by [[Circuit]]. He has the ability to interfere with game mechanics to some extent; not as extensive as Integrity, but he is capable of preventing players from sleeping via the [[Err.sleep|err.endisnear]] error, and causes [[minecraft.chatengine]] failures as well. The full extent of his power and abilities are not fully known, but judging by [[Revuxor]]'s intervention when the player is killed by The Broken End (prior to 2.0), he is capable of causing some sort of irreversible damage to players. On the [[Lore|Clan Server]], The Broken End first appeared on 01.11.2018, when his arrival caused the server's chat to malfunction. No one was able to talk to one another, and players were forced to communicate through signs. He then ambushed [[XXram2dieXx_(Lore)|xXram2dieXx]] on 04.11.2018, killing him. == Appearance == The Broken End is a towering, pitch-black, entity made of void tendrils; many of which drape, making him appear particularly unkempt when compared to other Void Creatures. He stands 36 blocks tall, and has an imperfect triangle-shaped head, as well as a smaller second head on his left shoulder, and another eye which hangs from the largest of his extra limbs. Though he resembles other Void Creatures in appearance, he is larger than the majority of them, and has what seems to be several additional malformed limbs coming out of his back. His right arm notably curls into a large, claw-like hook at the end. He has a single white dot for an eye in the middle of his main head. When enraged, that white dot shatters; being replaced shortly after by numerous red eyes, chaotically scattered across his entire face. From v1.1 to v1.8, The Broken End was 15 blocks tall. From v1.9 to v1.10.1, he was 22 blocks tall. == Personality == {{Quote | text = Administration. | author = [[Circuit]] when The Broken End is spoken about in chat. }} As seemingly the primary enforcer and right-hand man to [[Integrity]], The Broken End is quite cold, malevolent, remorseless, and unforgiving. He appears to be quite calculating, stripping away his victims' agency (such as causing Minecraft's chat engine to fail) before killing them. The Broken End lacks any semblance of empathy, mercy, or remorse. He is highly vindictive, particularly toward those he deems "traitors." == Behaviour == The Broken End can only spawn during the second stage of [[the Moon]]'s corruption, though his lures can spawn during the day. While The Broken End is present, he will turn the time to night, and it will start raining. The player will receive an [[err.endisnear]] error when attempting to sleep, and a [[minecraft.chatengine]] failure when attempting to send a chat message. === Stalk === The Broken End will spawn standing on the ground and watching the player. His appearance will be accompanied by a sudden '''onset of rain''', and '''halting of the daylight cycle'''; setting the doDaylightCycle gamerule to false. If the player looks at The Broken End while within '''75 blocks''' of him, he will disappear, and one of the following will happen: * With a {{tooltip|70%|7 in 10}} chance, he will reappear in his '''Chase''' behaviour after {{tooltip|25 seconds|500 ticks}}. * With a {{tooltip|30%|3 in 10}} chance, a [[Items#Physical Stacktrace|Physical Stacktrace]] block will replace the block he stood on. He will disappear {{tooltip|360 seconds|7200 ticks}} after he spawns, setting the doDaylightCycle gamerule back to true. === Chase === When The Broken End appears, the following will happen: tbe_intro.ogg'''tbe_intro.ogg''' will play, and the time of day is set to '''midnight'''. The Pause Menu will shake when opened, and pressing the '''Save and Quit to Title''' button will cause it to break and fall off. Once the Broken End begins to chase the Player, the_broken_end_chase.ogg'''the_broken_end_chase.ogg''' will start playing during the duration of the chase. The Broken End walking across water and '''breaking most blocks''' in his path to get to the Player, with the exception of some natural blocks such as dirt and stone. The Broken End will give the Player the '''Mining Fatigue II''' effect during the chase. * This stacks with the '''Darkness''' effect given by his stalk and ambush behaviors. Attempting to attack The Broken End will result in the Player taking {{tooltip|5 hearts|10 HP}} of damage '''without armor''' and knockback. Nearby iron golems will take major damage over time, quickly killing them. Boats within a 20-block-radius of The Broken End '''will be destroyed'''. The Player's screen will be covered by an animated black web which rapidly changes, significantly obscuring the player's vision.
[[File:TheBrokenEndDotScreenExample.png|border|245px|none]]
[[File:dotscreenframe.gif|border|260px]]
Every {{tooltip|7.5 seconds|150 ticks}} each of the following will happen: * theendisnear.ogg'''theendisnear.ogg''' will play with a heavy reverb effect, turning the sound into a growl; * With a 70% chance, a small black box will appear at the bottom of the screen for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}, and the time of day will be set to midnight; * With a 70% chance, a small black box will appear at the right side of the screen for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}, and the time of day will be set to day; * With a 70% chance, an image with the words “'''WE CAN HEAR YOU”''' will appear on the player's screen for {{tooltip|0.5 seconds|10 ticks}}, and the time of day will be set to noon; [[File:Wecanhearyou.png|border|200px]] When the player is killed by The Broken End, they will receive a death message reading "[player]'s time here has ended." He will disappear {{tooltip|50 seconds|1000 ticks}} after spawning. === Ambush === The Broken End will appear puppeteering a player, dangling what appears to be the corpse of said player from the end of a void tendril. The player being puppeted has several variants, adopt one of three players' names and skins at random: [[Not_It_Cal]] (50%), [[uImmortal_]] (25%), or [[TeChFella_99]] (25%). If the Player approaches the lure, the puppeted player will be pulled into the sky accommodated by the sound reel.ogg'''reel.ogg'''. The Broken End will appear behind the Player, entering his [[#Chase|Chase]] behavior. Every variant can be spawned using the NBT tag "variant", and the custom name can be changed with the NBT tag "CustomName". Running the command /summon thebrokenscript:the_broken_end_ambush ~ ~ ~ {CustomName:"Custom_Name_Here", variant: <1-3>} will spawn a desired variant of The Broken End - Ambush [[File:TheBrokenEndLure.png|border|400px|none]] [[File:TBEAmbush.gif|border|400x400px|The Broken End spawning behind the player after they got too close to the bait.]] === Curious === From a random event, The Broken End will appear 75 ~ 110 blocks away from the player, standing and facing a random direction. If the player is not looking at The Broken End, it will begin to walk towards the player. Once The Broken End has been seen by the player for a cumulative {{tooltip|3 seconds|60 ticks}}, the following happens: * It disappears after flickering the text "I see you", turning the player's view towards where he was, briefly blinding the Player, and playing tbespawn1.ogg'''tbespawn1.ogg'''. * If he is within 50 blocks of the player, there is a {{tooltip|1%|1 in 100}} chance to change into his [[#Chase|Chase]] behavior at its location. Being within 40 blocks of the player also counts as being seen, as does having The Broken End within the player's view cone or directly under the player's crosshair. [[File:TBE Curious Encounter.mp4|border|400px]] He will disappear {{tooltip|120 seconds|2400 ticks}} after he spawns if none of these behaviours happen. == Special Summoning == Aside from natural spawning, there is another way to summon The Broken End: '''Mall structure summoning'''. While within 15 blocks of a [[Structures#Mall|mall]] structure, the Player can say the trigger phrase {{tooltip|Not_It_Cal|Capitalization is ignored, spaces are treated as _.}}. At this point, Null must have joined, and there must be no active summon Clan Build structure within 100 blocks of the player — if there is one, the very same trigger phrases will summon [[Curved]] instead. After {{tooltip|5 seconds|100 ticks}}, The Broken End Ambush will be summoned at a random direction 50–100 blocks away from the player. What it does afterwards is covered above. [[File:Mall.png|thumb|none|mall]] '''This method can only work once every structure.''' == Notes == * Though Void Creatures canonically lack gender identities or a biological sex, The Broken End is referred to as he/him pronouns by the developers. * The Broken End's speech, thebrokenendspeech.ogg'''thebrokenendspeech.ogg''', was revealed by wendigodrip, where he monologues about the fate of previous players. ** The speech has not been added in 2.0, however, is confirmed by the developers that it will eventually be added with a new voice. * Prior to 2.0, the spread of [[Items#Physical Stacktrace|Physical Stacktrace]] blocks could be stopped by quickly removing the blocks on the same layer before the spread becomes unmanageable. ** In 2.0, the spread of [[Items#Physical Stacktrace|Physical Stacktrace]] blocks can no longer be prevented, as they will spread through the entirety of the Y-level. pages.title: The Broken Script
pages.extract:
The Broken Script is a mod that has numerous entities haunting it in addition to glitches in both the visual and technical aspects. The experiences of each player will be distinct, as if this mod has its own will. In other words, each player will have a different experience. The [[entities]] that are present vary in their levels of hostility and passiveness, ultimately corrupting the world. If the [[Frequently Asked Questions#Can I lose my world?|safemode]] is not utilized, players may be “banned” from their world. Since communications with the entities within the mod seem to be at best limited and at worst nonexistent, most of what is known about The Broken Script comes from inferred information. Except for [[Null]], who seems open to talking, but only to a certain point. The client is immediately noticeably off after the Broken Script is installed and Minecraft is launched. The music that plays on the title screen is eerie, and the game cannot be quit through the menu. Consequently, the default Minecraft splash texts are at best ominous and at worst threatening. Information about said corruption of the Minecraft client can be found in [[Lore]]. Further investigation indicates that the source of corruption appears to be hidden within another mod called [[Spectrum_11]]. Spectrum_11, which was initially discovered in the Broken Script files, appears to be absent from version 1.9.3. [https://discord.com/channels/1346186348251316346/1346205109310197841/1348761051386220606 Wendigo is kind enough to share this extra mod on his official Discord server], but players should be aware that it is invasive. Players are advised to refrain from opening a world that contains spectrum_11 in their client, as recommended by this wiki community. '''Do not play with spectrum_11 unless you are prepared for the consequences of your actions.''' = Publication History = The Broken Script, a horror mod for Minecraft, has generated a lot of controversy. Before it was taken down from CurseForge, The Broken Script was already well-known in the modding community for its unique take on horror. Its popularity skyrocketed after its removal from CurseForge. Some individuals who were misinformed decided to report The Broken Script as malware and have the mod removed from CurseForge. Following that, it was moved to Modrinth. Version 1.8 did not have what Version 1.9 had. The void's control seemed more severe in version 1.9 and the most severe influence the mod had been the ability to send a command to turn off the player's PC. The command itself is simply the equivalent of pressing the power button; however, this action scared a large majority of individuals who wished to play the Broken Script. This fear turned into unwarranted hostility, harassment, and death threats sent towards wendigodrip. Following this, the mod was removed from the public. Upon further investigation, it was discovered that the 1.9 version of the Broken Script is capable of only three functions: creating a single.txt file on the player's desktop, turning off the PC, and displaying Lightweight Java Game Library (LWJGL) pop-ups for [[err.sleep]]. The video “corruption” that resulted from the PC shutdown for those recording was not intentional; rather, it was the result of the recording program's inability to process and save the footage. Following this, a [[discordinvite:aPEryXpd|community patch]] was made. = Present days = The mod is currently being actively published on Modrinth. All the versions that have been released on Modrinth are not considered ‘unsafe’ for computers and can be used by the player without any issues. You can find older ‘unsafe’ versions on the official Discord. Further development does no longer incorporate invasive elements, and those who wish to irritate their nerves and their operating system may install the previous builds. As of recent wedigodrip has left the development team due to burnout. he has confirmed that other mods of his will still be developed he is simply taking a break. as of now development is being lead by redstonewizard.
{{Wiki navbox}}

{{Main page box/start | title = The Broken Script }} == The World They Built. The World They Hate. ==
''[[The Broken Script]]'' is a fantastic masterpiece of a horror mod provided by '''wendigodrip'''. This mod is capable of running commands on Windows and Linux systems, creating text files on desktops and causing Lightweight Java Game Library (LWJGL) Alerts to pop up during gameplay. Effectively, ''[[The Broken Script]]'' is an ARG. The story and atmosphere of ''The Broken Script'' is reminiscent of old Minecraft ARGs and Creepypastas. Most notably that of VoidExp (by mark101). However, ''The Broken Script'' has entities and events of it's own, the story within the Broken Script is separate from that of Mark101's series. Frequent questions have answers [[Frequently Asked Questions|here]].

pages.title: The Moon
pages.extract:
{{Distinguish|text = [[Moon]], a dimension}} The '''Moon''' is a celestial body that appears in the night sky. It plays an important role both in gameplay and [[lore]] of The Broken Script. [https://minecraft.wiki/w/Moon#Phases Click here to learn more about Minecraft Moon Phases] At the start of the game, the moon looks and behaves as normal. However, as part of a related [[Random_Events#Moon_Phase|random event]], if the current moon phase is 1 - '''Full Moon''', then the Moon moves to the next stage of '''Corruption'''. The '''Corruption''' is visually represented by different moon textures for each stage, depicting it being slowly consumed by the '''Void''' more and more with each passing night. It is speculated that this process has some connection to [[The Broken End]], as the corrupted moon has similar eyes, and the '''second stage of corruption''' is a direct requirement for him to spawn. Regardless of Corruption, during '''moon phases 4-7''' (New Moon - Waxing Gibbous) some hostile mobs '''cannot spawn''', making the nights quieter in this regard, but ultimately just giving more space for [[entities]] to spawn. This also affects the Nether and End. There is also a '''50%''' chance of receiving [[err.themoon]] when trying to sleep during these phases. ''Note: Phase 4 (New Moon) is also likely meant to have these behaviors, but does not due to a coding oversight.'' Despawnable Mobs: * Skeleton * Skeleton Horse * Zombie * Zombie Horse * Zombie Villager * Creeper * Bat * Spider * Cave Spider * Enderman * Witch == Corruption Stage 1 Phases == === Phase 1 === The moon initially looks normal aside from a faint crack. When the time reaches midnight, a sound similar to a crack and a static is played titled the_moon.ogg'''the_moon.ogg''', the tendrils of corruption burst and cracks the Moon. [[File:Moon_1_clean.png|border|200px]][[File:Moon_crack.gif|border|200px|The moon cracking.]][[File:Moon_1.png|border|200px]] === Phase 2 === The tendrils that previously appeared have now gotten a bigger grasp at the moon, to the point of causing it to dim. [[File:moon_2.png|border|200px]] === Phase 3 === The moon now appears to emanate a faint red glow, and the tendrils have expanded slightly. [[File:moon_3.png|border|200px]] === Phase 4 === The moon is now facing the world directly, and is pulsing a bright red light. The tendrils have also gotten a bigger grasp on the moon, almost fully taking it over. [[File:Moon_4_clean.png|border|200px]][[File:Moon_pulse.gif|border|200px]][[File:Moon_4.png|border|200px]] === Phase 5 === While mostly resembling the night before, the mass has expanded slightly - with a couple more thick tendrils and a larger centre, within which a bright red dot is present, accompanied by another dim speck on its left. Aforementioned entities will despawn at this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:Moon_5.png|border|200px]] === Phase 6 === There is nothing in the sky except the stars. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:Moon_6.png|border|200px]] === Phase 7 === The mass is back, with smaller gaps between the tendrils and now sporting a multitude of small red "eyes", looking almost like it is infested. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:Moon_7.png|border|200px]] === Phase 8 === The tendrils seem to have agglomerated into one large mass with 4 distinct eyes, bearing a striking resemblance to the eyes of [[Integrity]] and [[The Broken End]] in their enraged states. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:Moon_8.png|border|200px]] == Corruption Stage 2 Phases == === Phase 1 === The black mass now has a more triangular shape, resembling [[Integrity]] and [[The Broken End]] even more. The red mass seem to have spread apart into random shapes and structures. Aforementioned entities begin spawning again. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase1.png|border|200px]] === Phase 2 === The moon appears to be a bright red, elongated slash or streak, with a smaller white streak embedded in it. Around the slash are what appears to be small red "eyes". [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase2.png|border|200px]] === Phase 3 === Similar to phase 2, but this slash is now white and slightly thicker, with more "eyes" surrounding it. The red glow has also faded to white. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase3.png|border|200px]] === Phase 4 === A singular white dot in the centre of a hardly-visible triangle, appearing very similar to the face of The Broken End. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase4.png|border|200px]] === Phase 5 === The white dot is surrounded by a red circle, resembling an eye. The faint red glow has also returned, although barely visible. Aforementioned entities will despawn at this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase5.png|border|200px]] === Phase 6 === The red circle has expanded, and now contains what seems to be a large pupil, accompanied by smaller eye-looking dots around it. The red glow has also gotten brighter. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase6.png|border|200px]] === Phase 7 === The red dots around the moon have faded, leaving the moon as an unrecognizable, flesh-like mass. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase7.png|border|200px]] === Phase 8 === Red dots have reappeared around the mass, lighting up each extremity. It looks similar to phase 7 of the last stage. Aforementioned entities will not spawn during this stage, and sleeping may show an [[err.themoon]] popup. [[File:CorruptionStage2Phase8.png|border|200px]] == Spawn Probability Matrix == Beyond its visual role, the Moon also functions as the '''central rhythm controller''' for nearly every Moon-dependent spawn event in the mod. Entities and events whose generation depends on the moon (including [[r2]], [[He]], [[The Broken End]], [[Nothingiswatching]], [[Fractured]], and [[Fever#Stalk|Fever]] all read from a single shared lookup table — a 3×8 matrix indexed by the current corruption stage and the current Minecraft moon phase. === How the matrix works === The matrix is a constant Array<FloatArray> defined inside the spawn-conditions class for each entity. Its semantics are the same across all callers: * '''Row''' = getMoonStage() (0/1/2) * '''Column''' = the mod-internal phase number (getMoonPhase() + 1), ranging from 1 (Full Moon) through 5 (New Moon) to 8 (Waxing Gibbous). See the numbering notes below for how this maps to Vanilla getMoonPhase() 0–7. * '''Value''' = the per-check acceptance probability. The check itself is random.nextFloat() > matrix[stage][phase] → rejected; otherwise the spawn proceeds to the next gate. === The full matrix === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |+ spawnChanceMatrix (shared 3×8 spawn weight table) ! Moon Corruption \ Phase ! 1 (Full Moon) ! 2 ! 3 ! 4 ! 5 (New Moon) ! 6 ! 7 ! 8 |- ! 0 (No Corruption) | 0.00% | 0.01% | 0.01% | 0.05% | 0.45% | 0.85% | 0.85% | 0.85% |- ! 1 (Stage 1 Corruption) | 0.10% | 0.20% | 0.20% | 0.50% | 0.85% | 0.90% | 1.00% | 1.00% |- ! 2 (Stage 2 Corruption) | 0.30% | 0.30% | 0.60% | 0.60% | 0.50% | 0.00% | 0.00% | 0.00% |} === Reading the matrix === At Moon Corruption Stage 0 the Full Moon never spawns anything — its cell is hard-coded to 0.00% — and the table only starts returning non-zero values once you cross into the latter half of the lunar cycle (Phases 5 through 8), topping out at 0.85% per check. At Stage 1, every phase becomes a viable spawn window; the Full Moon rises from zero to 0.10% per check, and the late-cycle phases (7 and 8) reach the matrix-wide ceiling of 1.00%. At Stage 2, the table does not keep broadening where it actually narrows back, with only the first half of the lunar cycle (Phases 1 through 5) carrying any weight, and the late-cycle phases dropping once more to 0.00%; the highest per-check probability at Stage 2 sits at 0.60%, on phases 3 and 4. The numbers above are the probability of acceptance on a single spawn-check, not the rate at which a player will see the entity appear in a given minute or night. Some entities layer their own filter on top of the matrix: [[r2]]'s [[He]] variant multiplies the result by an extra 10% roll (so [[He]] appears roughly an order of magnitude less often than r2 in identical conditions), and [[The Broken End]] additionally requires moonStage == 2 regardless of which matrix cell would otherwise be read. === Who actually uses the matrix === Each spawn-conditions class either reads from the same 3×8 table or from a simplified 1D variant indexed only by moon stage: {| class="wikitable" |+ Spawn-condition classes referencing moonStage / spawnChanceMatrix ! Entity / event ! Source class ! How it uses the matrix |- ! [[r2]] / [[He]] / Stare | SiluetConditions | Reads matrix[moonStage][moonPhase] directly |- ! [[The Broken End]] | TBEConditions | Reads the matrix, then rejects unless moonStage == 2 |- ! [[Nothingiswatching]] | NIWConditions | Reads the matrix, then rejects unless moonStage == 0 |- ! [[Fractured]] | FracturedConditions | Uses a 1D FloatArray indexed by moonStage only |- ! [[Fever#Stalk|Fever]] | FeverStalkConditions | Same 1D FloatArray, indexed by moonStage only |} === Notes === * Phase numbering on this page uses the mod-internal scheme (getMoonPhase() + 1), in which Phase 1 = Full Moon and Phase 5 = New Moon; the underlying code uses Vanilla 0–7. Where the two systems collide — e.g. when citing getMoonPhase() + 1 == 1 directly — the relevant 0 in the Vanilla check corresponds to Phase 1 on this page. == Gallery == Current = File:Moon_crack.gif|The moon getting cracked at the start of stage 1. File:Moon_pulse.gif|The moon pulsing during phase 4 of stage 1. File:moon_phases1.png|Static Corruption Stage 1 phases. File:moon_phases2.png|Static Corruption Stage 2 phases. |-| Old = File:moon_phases_full.png|The old stage 1 phases from 1.10. File:moon_phases_2.png|The old stage 2 phases from 1.10. File:old_moon_phases_full.png|The older moon phases from 1.8. {{Clear}}

'''The Obliteration''' is the name given to two large geometric-shaped anomalies that cause severe effects when triggered.

It's unknown whether both Obliteration 1 and 2 are the same entity or not. It's also unknown if these two are former player(s), or if they're sentient void objects/masses (similar to [[Sub Anomaly 1]]) 

== Appearance ==
Obliteration 1 takes the form of a large, three-dimensional, star-shaped object with a hitbox of approximately '''12×14 blocks'''.

Obliteration 2 takes the form of a much larger inverted pyramid, with thin tendrils hanging beneath it, similar to the ones found on [[Void|void entities]]. Both Obliteration 1 and 2 are entirely pitch black in color.

Obliteration 1 is completely static until triggered, hovering unnaturally in midair, whereas Obliteration 2 glitches, warps, and moves in the sky constantly, following the Player when they are not under a cover. Interestingly, when walking away from Obliteration 2, it is affected by render distance much like terrain; which is peculiar for an entity, as normally they'd simply unload and stop rendering.

== Stats ==
Both variants share the following base values:
* '''Max HP''': 910 (455 hearts)
* '''Movement speed''': 1
* '''Hitbox''': 12×14
* '''Armor''': 0
* Immune to fire/lava damage

== Spawn ==
Obliteration cannot spawn on its own and is only triggered by random events within the mod. The spawn conditions are strict:
* '''Difficulty''': Non-Peaceful
* '''World state''': Null has joined
* '''Boss fight''': Will not spawn during [[Integrity#Phase 1|Integrity Boss Phase 1]]
* '''Dimension''': Overworld only
* '''Sky light''': Must be greater than 0 (outdoors)
* '''Time''': Daytime only
* '''Probability''': approximately 1/118 (1/1000 in Superflat worlds)
* '''Cooldown''': Will not spawn again within the same world for {{tooltip|26 minutes and 40 seconds|32000 ticks}}
* '''Uniqueness''': No other Obliteration entity within 512 blocks

== Behavior ==
=== The Star ===
Obliteration in this state will float motionlessly around 25 blocks above where it spawns, and will not actively harm the Player unless triggered in some way. Inversely, the Player cannot harm Obliteration in any way.

==== Rising Phase ====
Obliteration can be triggered through two methods, both gradually accumulating an "alertness" meter, maxing out after {{tooltip|4 seconds|80 ticks}}.
* If the Player looks at Obliteration.
* If the Player is within 20 blocks of Obliteration.
If the Player stops triggering Obliteration through either method, this meter will drain twice as fast as it filled.

Once Obliteration enters its rising phase, it will identify the Player responsible and target only this Player, ascending and eerily twitching for {{tooltip|7.5 second|150 ticks}}. During this animation, <ab>vhs_scratch.ogg</ab>'''vhs_scratch.ogg''' will begin playing. Once completed, Obliteration will disappear.

==== VHS Phase ====
[[File:Err.player.png|thumb|LWJGL Error given when Obliteration 1 attempts to crash the game.]]
Obliteration's disappearance is indicated by the Player's screen being changed to use a VHS effect, as well as 60 {{particle icon|null_particle}}null particles appearing at the Player's location. Additionally, the [[Mechanics#Window Title|game window]] will now read "You are not welcome here".

Attempting to break or place blocks, interact with entities or blocks, or [[Mechanics#Broken Pause Menu|Pause or Quit]] the game will result in these actions ultimately failing.

The VHS effect lasts for {{tooltip|50 seconds|1000 ticks}}, with <ab>tape_hiss.ogg</ab>'''tape_hiss.ogg''' playing during the same duration.

Once the effect ends, one of the following can occur:
* Obliteration will crash the Player's game (If enabled), and causing an [[err.player]] popup will appear.
* Obliteration will kick the Player from their world.
* Nothing will happen.

Anything changed in the world during the VHS phase will return back to normal, as though it never happened.

If left untriggered, Obliteration will despawn after {{tooltip|210 seconds|4200 ticks}}.

=== Inverted Pyramid ===
Obliteration rise from the ground up until it enters the skies, where it will begin to hover around Y level 135.

It will start scanning for the nearest Player within 127.5 blocks. Once it finds a target, Obliteration will begin tracking that Player.

Obliteration will begin to chase the Player in the direction that it last saw them, stopping the chase if within {{tooltip|2 blocks|Ignores Y level}} of the Player's last location, '''regardless of the Player's gamemode'''.

If a Player is underneath Obliteration and shares a direct line of sight with it, then Obliteration will stay in place and begin to distort the Player's screen, increasing an internal timer by 1. Once this timer reaches {{tooltip|5 seconds|100 ticks}}, Obliteration will kick the Player from their world. It will remove itself within {{tooltip|2 seconds|40 ticks}} once the Player rejoins their world.

If the Player is under a non-transparent block, or is above Obliteration, it will instead begin searching for a new target. If the Player has Obliteration in their field of view while within 127.5 blocks, it will immediately begin to chase the Player again. 

If it fails to find a Player to distort, Obliteration will despawn after {{tooltip|210 seconds|4200 ticks}}.

== Notes ==
* In version 1.4 of the mod, Obliteration was a WIP entity that would directly crash the game. Obliteration wasn't fully implemented until the ''2.0 Update''

pages.title: Void
pages.extract:
[[File:TheVoid.png|thumb|200px|"The Void" in the third phase of the Integrity Bossfight.]] The '''Void''' is a sentient substance originating from somewhere in Space. Through the proxy of [[Entities#Void_Creatures|Void Creatures]], it is one of the primary focus points of [[The Broken Script]] and is the overarching antagonist of the story. As physical matter the Void seems to be able to exist across multiple states, appearing both in real life and digitally. It is very likely that all Void Creatures seen in Minecraft are also made of it. It is pitch black in color with red as a secondary color, often present in accents and eyes. Additionally, it seems to naturally gravitate towards a chaotic tendril-like and spiky look. During the Phase 3 bossfight of Integrity, if the player goes too high up into the air they'll be killed and their screen closed horizontally to pitch-black with the death message "(player) is no more." After defeating Integrity, the Void sends one of its tendrils down to take him and the player into itself, implying the player's death. == Origin == [[File:Void.8z_Ic2mf.png|thumb|200px|Cosmic voids map presented by Revuxor in his post.]] There have been attempts of figuring out what the "Void" is by characters such as [[Revuxor (Lore)|Revuxor]]. The main connection, possibly explaining the origin of the Void, was made by him with the cosmic voids. I keep hearing mentions of the “Void” in my head. Whenever I play this game, it’s like something is whispering secrets I shouldn’t know. Trying to scare me. But as someone who is in college focusing on space, I have to think of a much scarier question. What is the void. Is it an entity? An object? An idea? [[File:Voidsatellite.png|thumb|200px|Hubble Space Telescope infected by the Void.]] Astronomers usually refer to the “void” as little spots of nothingness in space. Areas where the universe is dark. I’ve mapped out all locations of where “voids” are located. But I don’t even know if that’s what the voices are even referring to. It could just mean “the absence of something” and not a physical place. Another connection to the void I maybe could see is the entity itself. It’s mostly black. The void usually means nothing. Black is associated with the absence of light, despite technically containing all colors of the visible light spectrum. Void also means zero in other languages. A lot of signs keep pointing to the fact that the void simply just means “the unknown”. I don’t think whatever this entity is wants us to know where it comes from. I am grasping at ideas but I feel if I don’t make sense of it now, I will go crazy in the end. This theory is plausible given the fact that the first documented encounter with the Void occured on October 13, 2010, when the Hubble Space Telescope was photographed covered in "black and red biomass", confirmed to be the Void. This predates all Minecraft-related incidents, suggesting that it indeed might have space-based origin, though the entity itself seems intent on keeping its exact nature ambiguous. == Goal == [[File:MoonView.png|thumb|200px|Infected Minecraft Moon.]] The Void's ultimate goal currently remains unclear, though its actions indicate an intent to spread and consume. Its behavior suggests a desire to infect and assimilate everything it comes into contact with, from physical and digital objects to [[Players|human victims]], who can be made into [[entities]] too. [[File:A_sight_to_behold.png|thumb|200px|left|A Sight To Behold.]] There seems to be a strong connection of the Void to the moon(s), given that [[the Moon]] is quickly infected in Minecraft, and the mod's endgame takes place literally on the [[Moon]] itself. If the image "A Sight To Behold." is to be taken directly, it seems that the Void's goal might be the consumption of the Moon and possibly the Earth as well. == Notes == # According to devs, the Void's design is based off of plants, fungi, and Eldrazi. ##Eldrazi (expand to see more)
are a fictional race in the universe of ''Magic: The Gathering'', the collectible card game, first introduced in the 2010 expansion set ''Rise of the Eldrazi''. They come from the Blind Eternities, the chaotic, logic-defying expanse that separates the planes, filled with raw aether, where ordinary beings are torn apart in an instant and only planeswalkers can survive for any length of time. Eldrazi are colossal predators that lurk in the void and feed on the mana and life energy of entire planes, leaving nothing but lifeless ruins in their wake, which is why they are described as a plague of locusts roaming the multiverse. They are led by three titans and, under the game's rules, belong to the colorless creature type.
##Some [[Entities#Void Entity|Void Entities]], including [[Fractured]] and [[Fever]], have some parts of their bodies that closely resemble the red spider lily (Lycoris radiata), a plant, which is closely tied to death, funerals, and the boundary between the living and the dead. Because its flowers bloom only after the leaves have withered, the two are said never to meet, making the plant a symbol of eternal separation and farewell. Also known as the "flower of the other shore", it is often linked to lost memories, the transience of life, and the journey of the dead. [[Category:Lore]]

Through the process of elimination, it can be easily speculated that he was the last member of [[Lore#xXram2dieXx's_Clan|xXram2dieXx's clan]] to be eradicated or influenced by the void. == Appearance == WHYER4 seemed to use a default Steve skin with a white shirt and blue pants. == Personality == From what can be read through signs left around the [[Clan Build|clan_build]] WHYER4 starts his sentences with a capital letter and often ends them without punctuation. He's seen to use abbreviations, and his writing can come off as a little childish. == Fate == {{Quote |text = ... |author = [[Null]] when spoken to about WHYER4 }} WHYER4's fate is currently unknown. {{Stub}} {{Infobox |title=WORLD2 |image=WORLD2 icon.png }} [[File:World2 Map 2.0.png|alt=|thumb|300x300px|The surface of WORLD2.]] '''WORLD2''' is a world save hidden on the forum. It depicts some parts of the territory of the server, and gives some more insight into The Broken Script's story. An important fact is that WORLD2 is '''not''' the original world of the [[Lore|server]], but only some chunks recovered from it, which represent exclusively the territory and surroundings of [[Clan Build]]. The world may be corrupted or otherwise anomalously affected, as it contains some oddities such as a stone cross, isolated corner stairs, and a snowy grass block with no snow on top. Due to the contradictory information presented in this world, it is impossible to say anything for sure about the time frame this world captures. While Clan Build is somewhere in the time span between [[Lore#06.09.2019_—_Deceiver_returns|Circuit's infiltration]] and [[Lore#xx.xx.xxxx_—_DyeXD412's_corruption|DyeXD412's corruption]], everything else, such as the signs containing the transcription of [[:File:record1.ogg|record1.ogg]] or warnings about [[Integrity]], leaves more questions than answers. It's worth noting that both WORLD2's '''icon.png''' and [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bGW25bKHgiM Playing_alone.mov] are from [[Faraway]]'s perspective. The implications or exact meaning of this are unknown at this time. == How to Find (2.0+) == The whole chain starts from [[Revuxor]]'s forum post http://localhost:2018/threads/Revuxor/there_is_time_to_stop_the_key_from_turning_. === Step 1- Hidden Link === At first glance, the text Revuxor posts appears nonsensical, especially the final two sentences (''time'' and ''lowered''), where Revuxor becomes extremely cryptic. [[File:Lower the case.png|thumb|none|Revuxor's Forum Post]] Opening the underlying HTML page with the browser's developer tools reveals a hidden link appended at the end of the document: 
files.mc-anomaly-archive.org/AAVAAVXAAFAGAVXVVFXDVXXGVAXVVGAGAVFAXAVXXXGXVAGGVGGVAGADAVGAVAF.zip
Immediately below the link, the page also exposes an alphabet: 
abcdefghijklmnopqwstuvwxyz1234567890
[[File:Gem-alert.png|thumb|none|Domain Expansion: Hidden Link]] === Step 2 - Identify the Cipher === The sublink AAVAAVXAAFAGAVXVVFXDVXXGVAXVVGAGAVFAXAVXXXGXVAGGVGGVAGADAVGAVAF is the cipher text of a ADFGVX cipher, as it only contains the 6 letters within the cipher's namesake. However, an ADFGVX cipher requires a password in addition to the ciphertext, as well as an alphabet, conveniently provided to us. === Step 3 - The Password === Revuxor's phrase ''Time is the key. The key is time;'' is the hint where the password comes from. Every post within this thread contains a different timestamp despite the Forum's traditional linear time progression. Ignoring all of the '''00:''' and ''':''' from each timestamp of Revuxor's posts produces the following string of numbers. 
25 05 19 20 05 18 04 01 25 20 15 04 01 25 01 14 04 20 15 13 15 18 18 15 23
By using an {{tooltip|A1Z26 cipher|A = 1, B = 2...Y = 25, Z = 26}} on each yields the following text: 
Y E S T E R D A Y T O D A Y A N D T O M O R R O W
If written without spaces, this will form a password usable for the above ADFGVX cipher. 
YESTERDAYTODAYANDTOMORROW
=== Step 4 - The Alphabet === With the password, everything the ADFGVX cipher needs has been gathered. However, the alphabet in Revuxor's post is invalid for an ADFGVX cipher. The letter '''R''' is missing, replaced with a '''W''', which appears twice. An ADFGVX Polybius square must contain each of the 36 characters '''exactly''' once, so the alphabet has to be repaired before decryption can proceed. === Step 5 - Decrypt and Complete === With a corrected alphabet and the password YESTERDAYTODAYANDTOMORROW, the ADFGVX decryption produces: 
E97A2DE884A5B8BCD4AA32842C84ED31
Revuxor's final clue was ''the case is lowered''. '''Lower the case.''' The actual plaintext is obtained by lowering the case of the new text: 
e97a2de884a5b8bcd4aa32842c84ed31
=== Step 6 - Download the Archive === Substitute the lowercase plaintext for the original ciphertext inside the URL: 
files.mc-anomaly-archive.org/e97a2de884a5b8bcd4aa32842c84ed31.zip
Visiting the corrected URL downloads the WORLD2 archive. == Accessing WORLD2 == == Players ==

xox_DisruptiveQuackle_xox |Profile=[http://localhost:2018/profile/Dairy_Queen Dairy_Queen] |Died=2024 (aged 28) |Affiliations= [[Lore#Blacklisted Clan|Blacklisted Clan]] }} xoxDairyQueen, known as Lucille Collins in real life, was the leader of [[Lore#Blacklisted Clan|Blacklisted Clan]]. == Appearance == xoxDairyQueen's Minecraft skin appears to fairly resemble her real life appearance, featuring blonde hair, a green and brown tunic, and black pants. She also wore glasses. == Personality == xoxDairyQueen is a person who likes reading, writing, Minecraft, art and delving into unnecessary rabbit holes. She wishes to be a writer but can't because she keeps "delving into the heinous crevices of this game", an addiction that will never be satiated. She is also an artist, and she is close to the members of Blacklisted. She can get irritated, or even pissed off pretty quickly. Lucy is autistic. [[File:loreisloreiguess.png|left|thumb|500x500px|She is autistic.]]
It's possible that during her time on the server, she was so passionate about the clans that she unknowingly was cruel to her friends. She often tries to rationalize things. Even when she is mad she can care. She wishes that she never played on the server along with the rest of Blacklisted. She has enough courage and dedication to interview a [[Fever|void entity]] for more than days. She cares a lot about Neb and Carlos but she only tolerates Dom because the other two like him. == Fate == === Do you miss me? === Found by clicking the word [[#her|her]] in the thread [[#@DJ2trappy2skeezy|@DJ2trappy2skeezy]]
"Hello, no one is available to take your call. Please leave a message after the tone." ['''Tone'''] Uhhh. Hey. Just calling cuz uh... DJ said you two still aren’t on talking terms? Look. I get it. He can be a massive pain in the ass sometimes, but he... Didn’t mean anything by it. I... think that the both of you need to get a grip? Sort it out like... Yknow, like adults? Um... I miss you. Hop back on with us. Cheers.
=== Forget it. ===
"Hello, no one is available to take your call. Please leave a message after the tone." ['''Tone'''] Neb? This is getting ridiculous now. You need to get some better friends because your CREATURE of a mate still ain’t willing to check in on you... Forget it! Forget it.
=== I hope it hurts. ===
"Hello, no one is available to take your call. Please leave a message after the tone." ['''Tone'''] It's your fucking fault. Every single bit of this is on YOU. I'll never understand how you changed EVERYTHING over what? 20 iron? Is that what you decided was worth throwing out 10 years of friendship for? You couldn't of just swallowed your pride for five minutes, oooh noo, you just HAD to throw your tantrum, disappear off the face of the earth, and leave the rest of us to deal with the wreckage. Here is the __, the real bone tickler... you w- you won't even speak to me anymore? Did you ran out to me and Immortal __, I mean, the guy was outright __ the server when I spoke to him last anyway, I might've well laughed because it was dying, then BOOM! Silence! haha.... fuck. Ten years. Ten fucking years. gone. All because YOU were too emotionally stunted, no, no, too CHILDISH to admit you were acting like an idiot. I defended you! Called you my friend, y'know, stood by you whilst I should've... I regret it. I regret every second of it. I regret ever meeting you. I regret ever saying you mattered to me. I regret believing you were my friend. Crying I hope, one day, this catches up with you. Karma will drag you down by the _ (scruff of the neck). I hope it hurts.

Do you understand how fiercely she fought?
Goodness, it was almost embarrassing. For someone who wore dignity so proudly, she surrendered it
with astonishing ease once confronted with the exquisite
reality of her situation. she thrashed until her limbs
wouldn't listen to her, instead muttering their own prayers,
while her nails kept raking against anything they could touch. I warned her so many times, you know. I told her. Yet she refused to see what I see. What we see. Most humans possess the grace to accept what is given to
them. They weep, bargain and then eventually succumb to their
fragile need to still. But, those tiresome little outliers
insist upon making a ceremony of it. All that kicking. all
that clawing. All that dreadful noise. And somehow, we are the cruel ones. Even at the end, she could not comprehend the honour bestowed
upon her. She bared her teeth and poured that relentless
venom upon the only being who had ever truly watched her. A
deity who had paid such tender attention to the last moments
of her miserable, mortal life. Such ingratitude. Still, there came a moment when her hands loosened. When her voice softened into nothing. When all that fury finally left her body, she became peaceful
despite herself.
Oh, well. The garden has never cared whether its fertiliser died
willingly, so why start now?

=== What it means to be lonely. === Found in the thread [http://localhost:2018/threads/Dairy_Queen/what_it_means_to_be_lonely_ What it means to be lonely.], dated May 14th, 2018.
Dairy_Queen: So, as I was drawing, I couldn’t help but notice how melancholic I had accidentally made the piece. It was initially meant to be a pose study featuring myself, but something about it had inspired me to do some writing alongside it. This is not Minecraft related, so feel free to scroll if you must. : ) — What does it '''truly''' mean to be lonely? Is it something as simple as absence; the empty space beside you, the voice that no longer answers when called. Or, is it merely another abstract terror hammered into our heads until we learn to perceive it as inherently bad? It has never sat right with me, this insistence that all loneliness must be a form of suffering. You could wander the eternal halls of purgatory, passing door after door without ever finding another soul behind them, and still remain content within your own skin. Your footsteps might be the only sound left in that endless place, but at least they would belong to you. At the end of it all, what truly matters is autonomy. The quiet certainty that your thoughts are your own, that your hands move because you command them to, that no one else has the right to decide what shape your life must take. This is why it '''vexes''' me when others claim we must belong to another when that is certainly not the case. We may offer pieces of ourselves. Our time, our trust, the softer parts we usually keep hidden; but no person can ever be promised to another. People leave. Sometimes through choice, sometimes through cruelty, and sometimes with such terrible suddenness that the warmth has not yet faded from their chair before the world begins referring to them in the past tense. One moment, they are speaking. The next, their mouth is still, their eyes fixed upon something no one else can see and every word you thought you still had time to say becomes useless inside you. That is the fragility of surrounding yourself with others. You mistake their presence as permanence. A coat left hanging by the door does not mean its owner will return, you know? The dead leave ordinary things behind and perhaps that is what makes death so obscene. Nothing announces itself. Clocks continue and rooms remain, the only difference being that the person is missing, excised so cleanly from the world that their absence begins to feel more tangible than they ever did. Yet, here you are. '''Left behind'''. You are the only person you are guaranteed to wake beside. Perhaps loneliness is merely a lie bestowed upon those who have yet to discover that kingdom. A fear placed carefully inside them so they might be moulded by whatever environment surrounds them. After all, someone terrified of being abandoned can be made to endure almost anything. They will surrender their voice, their dignity, even the boundaries of their own body; provided someone promises not to leave. We are social creatures by nature, of course. Some ancient part of us still understands isolation as a death sentence. If we were left to fend for ourselves by firelight, with no signs of those who hunt and gather or the mothers that would keep our bodies warm, we would surely succumb to the beasts of the night. Funny how we now have to fear other beasts. Man is corrupt. Man stigmatises what he cannot understand and shames whatever obstructs the finality of his blueprint. He calls solitude sickness because he cannot tolerate the possibility that another person might not need him. He teaches us to fear an empty room, when perhaps what truly frightens him is someone who can sit within it undisturbed. I do not wish to be lonely. I only think people should become more comfortable with absence. With empty chairs, cold bedsides and the possibility that those they love may be taken without warning. There may come a day when every familiar voice has fallen quiet. When I walk through rooms once crowded with life and find that only my footsteps answer me. Since xXram2dieXx's consciousness is preserved in the form of [[Null]], it is unknown for sure what exactly this anomaly is. == Appearance == xXram2dieXx appears to be very similar to [[Null]], with some pieces of his original Minecraft skin shown in the face instead of the full pitch-black face [[Null]] has. == Behaviour == After breaking a [[Items#Hello|Hello]] block, xXram2dieXx will be able to join the world. He can only join once per world. Upon spawning in, a message will be sent in chat, with the word "web" obfuscated, hinting towards accessing the [[Forum]]s Local g w a e m b e hosted on port [2018] After 25 seconds, time of the day will be faked to midnight, an eerie noise will play, followed by a new message in chat. xXram2dieXx joined the game After 25 seconds, time of the day will be faked to midnight again. {{tooltip|48656c6c6f3f|Hello?}} After 25 seconds, time of the day will be faked to midnight once more. {{tooltip|486f772064696420796f752066696e642074686973207365727665723f|How did you find this server?}} After 25 seconds, time of the day will be faked to day. {{tooltip|446f20796f752077616e7420746f20626520667269656e64733f|Do you want to be friends?}} After 25 seconds, time of the day will be faked to night. {{tooltip|4c656176652e|Leave.}} After 25 seconds, xXram2dieXx will leave the game. xXram2dieXx left the game If at any point the player comes within 20 blocks of xXram2dieXx, he will disappear and one of the following will happen: * With a {{tooltip|70%|7 in 10}} chance, [[Null]] will appear in xXram2dieXx's place in his [[Null#Chase|Chase]] behavior. * With a {{tooltip|30%|3 in 10}} chance, the player will be [[Banning|banned]] from the world. He instantly disappears during the day. == Notes == * Seems quite friendly in text. * In [[WORLD2]] xXram2dieXx's former (or temporary) clan build has a little minecart ride inside of it, it is being assumed that xXram2dieXx built it. This little structure is entirely impractical, completely useless, loops in a tiny 2x2 circular rail track… and it's the most adorable thing ever. == Media == File:Ram2die transparent.png|Transparent xXram2dieXx Render File:Xxram2diexxtbsRender.png|Artistic Render [[Category:Entities]] {{Wiki navbox}} {{DISPLAYTITLE:xXram2dieXx}}
